sentences.zh: 梁士彥梁士彥，字相如，安定烏氏人也。

translations.literal: Liang Shiyan, styled Xiangru, was a man of Wushi in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shiyan, whose style name was Xiangru, came from Wushi in Anding.

sentences.zh: 少任俠，不仕州郡。

translations.literal: In youth he was chivalrous and would not serve in prefectures or commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he lived by the code of the knight-errant and refused office in the local administration.

sentences.zh: 性剛果，喜正人之是非。

translations.literal: His nature was firm and resolute; he delighted in setting right the rights and wrongs of others.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and decisive by nature and took pleasure in judging the rights and wrongs of other men.

sentences.zh: 好讀兵書，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: He loved reading military books and had considerable acquaintance with the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of military treatises and had read widely in the classics and histories as well.

sentences.zh: 周世以軍功拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the Zhou era he was appointed Yitong Sanqi on account of military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Zhou he was enfeoffed as Yitong Sanqi for his achievements in war.

sentences.zh: 武帝將有事東夏，聞其勇決，自扶風郡守除九曲鎮將，進位上開府，封建威縣公，齊人甚憚焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was about to undertake affairs in Eastern Xia, hearing of his courage and decisiveness, he removed him from the post of Fufeng prefect to make him commander of Jiuqu Fortress, advanced him to Shang Kaifu, enfeoffed him as Duke of Jianwei County, and the men of Qi feared him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was preparing his campaign against the eastern Qi state, he heard of Shiyan’s courage and resolution, transferred him from prefect of Fufeng to commander of Jiuqu Fortress, promoted him to Shang Kaifu, and created him Duke of Jianwei—so greatly did the Qi fear him.

sentences.zh: 尋遷熊州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to be governor of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was moved to the governorship of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 後從武帝拔晉州，進位柱國，除使持節、晉絳二州諸軍事、晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Wu in capturing Jinzhou, was advanced to Pillar of State, and was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the two prefectures of Jin and Jiang, and Governor of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Emperor Wu in the capture of Jinzhou, was raised to Pillar of State, and was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, supreme commander of military affairs in Jin and Jiang, and governor of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 及帝還後，齊後主親總六軍而圍之。

translations.literal: When the emperor had returned to the rear, the Qi sovereign personally took command of the six armies and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor had withdrawn to the rear, the Qi sovereign personally led the six armies and laid siege to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 獨守孤城，外無聲援，眾皆震懼，士彥慷慨自若。

translations.literal: He alone defended the isolated city; there was no support from outside; the masses were all shaken with fear, but Shiyan was generous and spirited as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan held the lone city with no relief from outside; his troops were terrified, yet he himself remained spirited and unshaken.

sentences.zh: 賊盡銳攻之，樓堞皆盡，城雉所存，尋仞而已。

translations.literal: The enemy attacked with all their strength; the towers and parapets were all destroyed; what remained of the battlements was only a few ren in height.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy threw their full strength against the walls until towers and parapets were gone and only a few feet of rampart remained.

sentences.zh: 或短兵相接，或交馬出入。

translations.literal: At times they closed in with short weapons; at times they charged in and out on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they fought hand to hand at the walls; sometimes they charged in and out on horseback.

sentences.zh: 士彥謂將士曰：「死在今日，吾為爾先！

translations.literal: Shiyan said to his officers and soldiers: "Death comes today—I shall go before you!
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan told his officers and men, "If we die today, I shall die before you!

sentences.zh: 」於是勇烈齊奮，呼聲動地，無不一當百。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the brave and fierce all strove together; their shouts shook the earth; not one failed to match a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: " At that every brave man charged as one; their battle cry shook the ground, and each fought as though he were worth a hundred.

sentences.zh: 齊師少卻。

translations.literal: The Qi army drew back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces fell back a little.

sentences.zh: 乃令妻妾軍民子女，晝夜修城，三日而就。

translations.literal: He then ordered wives, concubines, soldiers, civilians, and children to repair the walls day and night; in three days it was done.
translations.idiomatic: He then set wives, soldiers, townspeople, and even children to repair the walls day and night, and in three days the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 帝率六軍亦至，齊師解圍，營於城東十餘裡。

translations.literal: The emperor also arrived leading the six armies; the Qi army lifted the siege and encamped more than ten li east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor arrived at the head of the six armies; the Qi lifted the siege and pitched camp more than ten li east of the city.

sentences.zh: 士彥見帝，持帝須而泣曰：「臣幾不見陛下！

translations.literal: When Shiyan saw the emperor, he seized the emperor’s beard and wept, saying: "Your servant almost failed to see Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: When Shiyan met the emperor he seized his beard and wept, saying, "Your servant nearly never saw Your Majesty again!

sentences.zh: 」帝亦為之流涕。

translations.literal: " The emperor also wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wept in turn.

sentences.zh: 時帝以將士疲倦，意欲班師。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor, because the officers and soldiers were weary, intended to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing his troops exhausted, meant to withdraw the army.

sentences.zh: 士彥叩馬諫曰：「今齊師遁，眾心皆動，因其懼也而攻之，其勢必舉。

translations.literal: Shiyan seized the horse’s bridle and remonstrated, saying: "Now the Qi army is in flight and every heart is unsettled; if we attack them while they are afraid, the enterprise is sure to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan seized the bridle of the emperor’s horse and urged him, "The Qi army is in flight and their morale is shaken; strike while they are afraid and victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，大軍遂進。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his advice, and the great army advanced.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took his counsel and the main force pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 帝執其手曰：「余之有晉州，為平齊之基。

translations.literal: The emperor took his hand and said: "My holding of Jinzhou is the foundation for pacifying Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his hand and said, "My possession of Jinzhou is the foundation for conquering Qi.

sentences.zh: 若不固守，則事不諧矣。

translations.literal: If it had not been firmly held, the affair would not have succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been held firm, the whole enterprise would have failed.

sentences.zh: 朕無前慮，惟恐後變，善為我守之。

translations.literal: I had no forethought beforehand and only feared trouble afterward—guard it well for me.
translations.idiomatic: I gave no thought beforehand and feared only what might come after—guard it well for me.

sentences.zh: 」及齊平，封郕國公，進位上柱國、雍州主簿。

translations.literal: " When Qi was pacified, he was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Xu, advanced to Supreme Pillar of State, and made Chief Clerk of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " When Qi fell he was created Duke of Xu, promoted to Supreme Pillar of State, and appointed chief clerk of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，除東南道行台、使持節、徐州總管、三十二州諸軍事、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan acceded, he was appointed Southeast Circuit Mobile Office, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Xuzhou, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in thirty-two prefectures, and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Shiyan was made commissioner of the Southeast Circuit, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, supreme commander of Xuzhou and thirty-two prefectures, and governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 與烏丸軌擒陳將吳明徹、裴忌于呂梁，別破黃陵，略定淮南地。

translations.literal: Together with Wuyan Gui he captured the Chen generals Wu Mingche and Pei Ji at Luliang, separately broke Huangling, and broadly pacified the Huainan region.
translations.idiomatic: With Wuyan Gui he captured the Chen generals Wu Mingche and Pei Ji at Luliang, took Huangling in a separate action, and brought most of the Huainan region under control.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，轉亳州總管、二十四州諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu served as Chancellor, Shiyan was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Bozhou and Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in twenty-four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became chancellor, Shiyan was transferred to supreme commander of Bozhou and military affairs in twenty-four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 尉迥之反也，以為行軍總管，從韋孝寬擊之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, he was made Campaign Commander-in-Chief and followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion, Shiyan was made campaign commander and marched with Wei Xiaokuan against him.

sentences.zh: 至河陽，與迥軍相對。

translations.literal: Reaching Heyang, he faced Jiong’s army.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyang he confronted Jiong’s forces.

sentences.zh: 令家僮梁默等數人為前鋒，士彥以其徒繼之，所當皆破。

translations.literal: He ordered several of his household retainers, including Liang Mo, to serve as vanguard; Shiyan followed with his own men, and wherever they met the enemy they broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his household retainer Liang Mo and a few others as vanguard; Shiyan followed with his own men and broke every force they met.

sentences.zh: 乘勝至草橋，迥眾複合，進戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory to Caoqiao, Jiong’s masses reassembled; they advanced to battle and were thoroughly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the victory to Caoqiao, they met Jiong’s troops re-formed for battle and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 及圍鄴城，攻北門而入，馳啟西門，納宇文忻之兵。

translations.literal: When they besieged Ye City, he attacked through the north gate and entered, then galloped to open the west gate and admit Yu Wenxin’s troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Ye he stormed the north gate, then galloped to open the west gate and let in Yu Wenxin’s troops.

sentences.zh: 及迥平，除相州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jiong was pacified, he was appointed Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong’s defeat he was made governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖忌之，未幾，征還京師，閒居無事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was wary of him; before long he was summoned back to the capital and lived in retirement with nothing to do.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor distrusted him; before long he was recalled to the capital and lived idle at home.

sentences.zh: 自恃元功，甚懷怨望，遂與宇文忻、劉昉等謀作亂。

translations.literal: Relying on his original merit, he harbored deep resentment and accordingly plotted rebellion with Yu Wenxin, Liu Fang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Counting on his founding merit, he nursed deep grievances and joined Yu Wenxin, Liu Fang, and others in plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 將率僮僕，於享廟之際，因車駕出，圖以發機。

translations.literal: He intended to lead his household servants at the time of the ancestral offering, when the imperial carriage went out, and planned to set the mechanism in motion.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to lead his household retainers at the imperial ancestral rites, when the emperor went out in his carriage, and strike at that moment.

sentences.zh: 複欲于蒲州起事，略取河北，捉黎陽關，塞河陽路，劫調布以為牟甲，募盜賊以為戰士。

translations.literal: He also wished to raise troops at Puzhou, seize Hebei in a raid, take Liyang Pass, block the Heyang road, plunder tax cloth for armor, and recruit bandits as fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: He also planned to rise at Puzhou, seize Hebei, hold Liyang Pass, block the Heyang route, seize tax grain and cloth for armor, and enlist bandits as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其甥裴通豫知其謀而奏之。

translations.literal: His nephew Pei Tongyu learned of the plot and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Pei Tongyu learned of the plot and reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 高祖未發其事，授晉州刺史，欲觀其意。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu did not expose the affair but appointed him Governor of Jinzhou, wishing to observe his intentions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not yet move against him but appointed him governor of Jinzhou to see what he would do.

sentences.zh: 士彥欣然謂昉等曰：「天也！

translations.literal: Shiyan said gladly to Fang and the others: "Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan said delightedly to Liu Fang and the rest, "Heaven itself!

sentences.zh: 」又請儀同薛摩兒為長史，高祖從之。

translations.literal: " He also requested the Yitong Xue Mo’er as chief administrator; Emperor Gaozu granted it.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked for the Yitong Xue Mo’er as his chief administrator, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 後與公卿朝謁，高祖令左右執士彥、忻、昉等於行間，詰之曰：「爾等欲反，何敢發此意？

translations.literal: Later, when he attended court with the nobles and ministers, Emperor Gaozu ordered attendants to seize Shiyan, Xin, Fang, and the others in the ranks and interrogate them, saying: "You wish to rebel—how dare you harbor such intent?
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a court audience with the nobles, the emperor had attendants seize Shiyan, Yu Wenxin, Liu Fang, and the others in the ranks and demand, "You plotted rebellion—how dare you conceive such a thing?

sentences.zh: 」初猶不伏，捕薛摩兒適至，於是庭對之。

translations.literal: " At first they still would not confess; when Xue Mo’er was captured and just arrived, they were confronted in court.
translations.idiomatic: " At first they still denied it; then Xue Mo’er was brought in under arrest and confronted them in open court.

sentences.zh: 摩兒具論始末，雲：「第二子剛垂泣苦諫，第三子叔諧曰：作猛獸要須成斑。

translations.literal: Mo’er set forth the whole course of events in detail, saying: "The second son Gang wept and remonstrated bitterly; the third son Shuxie said: To make a fierce beast you must finish its stripes.
translations.idiomatic: Mo’er recounted the whole affair, saying, "The second son Gang wept and pleaded against it; the third son Shuxie said, To raise a fierce beast you must finish its stripes.

sentences.zh: 」士彥失色，顧謂摩兒曰：「汝殺我！

translations.literal: " Shiyan changed color and turned to Mo’er, saying: "You have killed me!
translations.idiomatic: " Shiyan turned pale and cried to Mo’er, "You have killed me!

sentences.zh: 」於是伏誅，時年七十二。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he confessed and was executed; he was seventy-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: " He then confessed and was put to death at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 有子五人。

translations.literal: He had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons.

sentences.zh: 操字孟德，出繼伯父，官至上開府、義鄉縣公、長寧王府驃騎，早卒。

translations.literal: Cao, styled Mengde, was given in adoption to his paternal uncle; his office reached Shang Kaifu, Duke of Yixiang County, and Biaoji of the Prince of Changning’s household; he died young.
translations.idiomatic: Cao, styled Mengde, was adopted by his uncle’s line, rose to Shang Kaifu, Duke of Yixiang, and biaoji to the Prince of Changning, and died young.

sentences.zh: 子剛剛字永固，弱冠授儀同，以平尉迥勳，加開府。

translations.literal: His son Gang, styled Yonggu, at the capping age was appointed Yitong; for merit in pacifying Yuchi Jiong he was given the additional title of Kaifu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gang, styled Yonggu, received the rank of Yitong at his capping; for service against Yuchi Jiong he was made Kaifu.

sentences.zh: 擊突厥有功，進位上大將軍、通政縣公、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit in attacking the Turks he was advanced to Supreme Great General, Duke of Tongzheng County, and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For victories over the Turks he was promoted to Supreme Great General, Duke of Tongzheng, and governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 士彥之誅也，以諫獲免，徙瓜州。

translations.literal: When Shiyan was executed, he was spared because of his remonstrance and was banished to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiyan was executed, Gang was spared for having remonstrated and was banished to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 叔諧官至上儀同、廣平縣公、車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Shuxie’s office reached Supreme Yitong, Duke of Guangping County, and General of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxie rose to Supreme Yitong, Duke of Guangping, and General of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 志遠為安定伯，務為建威伯，皆坐士彥誅。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan was made Baron of Anding; Wu was made Baron of Jianwei; both were implicated in Shiyan’s execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan was Baron of Anding and Wu Baron of Jianwei; both were executed because of Shiyan’s crime.

sentences.zh: 梁默梁默者，士彥之蒼頭，驍武絕人。

translations.literal: Liang Mo—Liang Mo was Shiyan’s personal slave; his martial valor was unmatched among men.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Mo was Shiyan’s household slave, a warrior without equal.

sentences.zh: 士彥每從征伐，常與默陷陣。

translations.literal: Whenever Shiyan went on campaign, Mo always broke the enemy lines with him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shiyan campaigned, Mo charged the enemy lines at his side.

sentences.zh: 仕周，致位開府。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he reached the rank of Kaifu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he rose to Kaifu.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，以行軍總管從楊素北征突厥，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaihuang era, as Campaign Commander-in-Chief he followed Yang Su on the northern expedition against the Turks and was advanced to Great General.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang reign he served as campaign commander under Yang Su against the Turks in the north and was promoted to Great General.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒之反也，複以行軍總管從楊素討平之，加授柱國。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Yang Liang rebelled, he again served as Campaign Commander-in-Chief following Yang Su to suppress and pacify him, and was further granted Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang of Han rebelled, he again followed Yang Su as campaign commander to crush the revolt and was further made Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，從煬帝征吐谷渾，遇賊力戰而死，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye, following Emperor Yang on the expedition against Tuyuhun, he met the enemy, fought fiercely, and died; he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 5 he followed Emperor Yang against Tuyuhun, fought the enemy to the death, and was posthumously made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 宇文忻宇文忻，字仲樂，本朔方人，徙京兆。

translations.literal: Yu Wenxin—Yu Wenxin, styled Zhongle, was originally a man of Shuofang and moved to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenxin, styled Zhongle, was originally from Shuofang but his family had moved to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖莫豆于，魏安平公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Modouyu was Duke of Anping of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Modouyu had been Duke of Anping under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父貴，周大司馬、許國公。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Grand Marshal of Zhou and Duke of the State of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui was Zhou’s grand marshal and Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 忻幼而敏慧，為兒童時，與群輩遊戲，輒為部伍，進止行列，無不用命，有識者見而異之。

translations.literal: Xin was clever and quick from childhood; when playing with his peers as a boy, he would always form them into units; in advance, halt, and formation none failed to obey—those with insight saw this and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was clever from childhood; even in play with other boys he would drill them into ranks, and none failed to obey his commands—men of discernment marked him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 年十二，能左右馳射，驍捷若飛。

translations.literal: At twelve he could shoot on horseback to left and right; his valor and agility were like flight.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could shoot from horseback to either side, swift as though he flew.

sentences.zh: 恆謂所親曰：「自古名將，唯以韓、白、衛、霍為美談，吾察其行事，未足多尚。

translations.literal: He constantly said to those close to him: "Among famous generals of antiquity, only Han Xin, Bai Qi, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing are held up for praise; when I examine their deeds, they are not especially worthy of admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He often told his intimates, "Men speak only of Han Xin, Bai Qi, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing among the great generals of old; when I weigh their deeds, they are not so very admirable.

sentences.zh: 若使與僕並時，不令豎子獨擅高名也。

translations.literal: If they had lived in my time, I would not have let those striplings monopolize high renown alone.
translations.idiomatic: Had they lived in my day, I would not have let those youngsters keep all the glory to themselves.

sentences.zh: 」其少小慷慨如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his generous spirit in youth.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the bold spirit of his boyhood.

sentences.zh: 年十八，從周齊王憲討突厥有功，拜儀同三司，賜爵興固縣公。

translations.literal: At eighteen he followed Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou in campaigning against the Turks with merit, was appointed Yitong Sanqi, and was granted the title Duke of Xinggu County.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he followed Prince Xian of Qi against the Turks with distinction, was made Yitong Sanqi, and created Duke of Xinggu.

sentences.zh: 韋孝寬之鎮玉壁也，以忻驍勇，請與同行。

translations.literal: When Wei Xiaokuan garrisoned Yubi, because of Xin’s valor he requested that Xin go with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Xiaokuan held Yubi, he asked to have the valiant Xin with him.

sentences.zh: 屢有戰功，加位開府、驃騎將軍，進爵化政郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He repeatedly won merit in battle, was given the additional ranks of Kaifu and General of Agile Cavalry, was advanced to Duke of Huazheng Commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He won repeated victories, was made Kaifu and General of Agile Cavalry, advanced to Duke of Huazheng with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 從武帝伐齊，攻拔晉州。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wu in the campaign against Qi and captured Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu against Qi and took Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊後主親馭六軍，兵勢甚盛，帝憚之，欲旋師。

translations.literal: The Qi sovereign personally drove the six armies; their military momentum was very strong; the emperor feared them and wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi sovereign personally led the six armies in overwhelming force; the emperor was afraid and meant to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 忻諫曰：「以陛下之聖武，乘敵人之荒縱，何往不克！

translations.literal: Xin remonstrated, saying: "With Your Majesty’s sacred martial prowess, riding the enemy’s dissipation and license—where would you not conquer!
translations.idiomatic: Xin urged him, "With Your Majesty’s sacred prowess, striking an enemy dissolute and reckless—where could you fail to prevail!

sentences.zh: 若使齊人更得令主，君臣協力，雖湯、武之勢，未易平也。

translations.literal: If the men of Qi should again obtain a worthy sovereign and ruler and minister join their strength, even the power of Tang and Wu would not easily pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: If Qi should again find a worthy ruler and court and sovereign worked as one, not even the might of Tang and Wu could easily subdue them.

sentences.zh: 今主暗臣愚，兵無鬥志，雖有百萬之眾，實為陛下奉耳。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign is dim and the ministers foolish; the troops have no fighting will—though they have a million men, in truth they are offered up to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: But now the ruler is dull and his ministers foolish; the army has no heart for battle. Though they number a million, they are in truth a gift to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，戰遂大克。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his advice, and the battle was thereupon a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took his counsel and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 及帝攻陷并州，先勝後敗，帝為賊所窘，左右皆殲，帝挺身而遁，諸將多勸帝還。

translations.literal: When the emperor stormed Bingzhou, he was victorious at first and defeated afterward; the emperor was cornered by the enemy; his attendants were all destroyed; the emperor broke through alone and fled; many generals urged the emperor to return.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor stormed Bingzhou he won at first and then lost; the enemy cornered him, his escort was wiped out, and he broke through alone while many generals urged retreat.

sentences.zh: 忻勃然而進曰：「自陛下克晉州，破高緯，乘勝逐北，以至於此。

translations.literal: Xin advanced with sudden anger and said: "Since Your Majesty captured Jinzhou, defeated Gao Wei, rode victory in pursuit to the north, and came to this point—
translations.idiomatic: Xin stepped forward angrily and said, "Since Your Majesty took Jinzhou, broke Gao Wei, and drove the victory north to this very place—

sentences.zh: 致令偽主奔波，關東響振，自古行兵用師，未有若斯之盛也。

translations.literal: —you have made the false sovereign flee in panic and the east of the passes resound with your fame; from antiquity in deploying armies and using forces, there has never been such splendor.
translations.idiomatic: you have put the false sovereign to flight and made the east of the passes tremble—never in history has an army marched in such glory.

sentences.zh: 昨日破城，將士輕敵，微有不利，何足為懷。

translations.literal: Yesterday’s storming of the city—the officers and soldiers treated the enemy lightly; there was a slight setback—what is there to brood over?
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday’s assault failed because the troops grew careless; a small setback is nothing to brood over.

sentences.zh: 丈夫當死中求生，敗中取勝。

translations.literal: A man should seek life in the midst of death and seize victory from defeat.
translations.idiomatic: A true man finds life in the jaws of death and wrests victory from defeat.

sentences.zh: 今者破竹，其勢已成，奈何棄之而去？

translations.literal: Now the bamboo is split—the momentum is already formed—how can you abandon it and leave?
translations.idiomatic: The bamboo is already split—the momentum is yours—how can you throw it away and turn back?

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言，明日複戰，遂拔晉陽。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his words; the next day they fought again and thereupon captured Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took his advice; the next day they fought again and took Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 及齊平，進位大將軍，賜物千段。

translations.literal: When Qi was pacified, he was advanced to Great General and granted a thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he was promoted to Great General and given a thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 尋與烏丸軌破陳將吳明徹于呂梁，進位柱國，賜奴婢二百口，除豫州總管。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, together with Wuyan Gui, he defeated the Chen general Wu Mingche at Luliang, was advanced to Pillar of State, was granted two hundred male and female slaves, and was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, with Wuyan Gui, he defeated the Chen general Wu Mingche at Luliang, was made Pillar of State, given two hundred slaves, and appointed supreme commander of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖龍潛時，與忻情好甚協，及為丞相，恩顧彌隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was still in obscurity, he and Xin were on very close terms; when he became Chancellor, favor and regard grew ever richer.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was still rising, he and Xin were close friends; once Yang Jian became chancellor, his favor toward Xin only deepened.

sentences.zh: 尉迥作亂，以忻為行軍總管，從韋孝寬擊之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong made rebellion, Xin was made Campaign Commander-in-Chief and followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Xin was made campaign commander and marched with Wei Xiaokuan against him.

sentences.zh: 時兵屯河陽，諸軍莫敢先進。

translations.literal: At that time the army was encamped at Heyang; none of the armies dared advance first.
translations.idiomatic: The army lay at Heyang and no unit dared advance.

sentences.zh: 帝令高熲馳驛監軍，與熲密謀進取者，唯忻而已。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Gao Jiong to ride post-horses to oversee the army; of those who secretly plotted advance with Jiong, only Xin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Gao Jiong by relay horse to supervise the army; of those who secretly planned the advance with Jiong, only Xin took part.

sentences.zh: 迥遣子惇，盛兵武陟，忻先鋒擊走之。

translations.literal: Jiong sent his son Dun with a strong force at Wuzhi; Xin as vanguard attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent his son Dun with a large force at Wuzhi; Xin as vanguard routed them.

sentences.zh: 進臨相州，迥遣精甲三千伏於野馬岡，欲邀官軍。

translations.literal: Advancing to Xiangzhou, Jiong sent three thousand picked armored troops to lie in ambush at Yema Hill, intending to intercept the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: As he advanced on Xiangzhou, Jiong hid three thousand picked troops at Yema Hill to ambush the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 忻以五百騎襲之，斬獲略盡。

translations.literal: Xin with five hundred horsemen raided them and killed or captured nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Xin fell on them with five hundred horsemen and killed or captured nearly every man.

sentences.zh: 進至草橋，迥又拒守，忻率奇兵擊破之，直趨鄴下。

translations.literal: Advancing to Caoqiao, Jiong again held defense; Xin led picked troops, broke them, and pressed straight to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At Caoqiao Jiong held the line again; Xin led picked troops, broke them, and drove straight for Ye.

sentences.zh: 迥背城結陣，與官軍大戰，官軍不利。

translations.literal: Jiong formed battle lines with his back to the city and fought a great battle with the imperial army; the imperial army fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong drew up his lines with his back to the city and fought a great battle; the imperial army fared badly.

sentences.zh: 時鄴城士女觀戰者數萬人，忻與高熲、李詢等謀曰：「事急矣，當以權道破之。

translations.literal: At that time tens of thousands of men and women of Ye watched the battle; Xin with Gao Jiong, Li Xun, and others plotted, saying: "The affair is urgent—we must use an expedient stratagem to break them.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of men and women of Ye were watching the battle; Xin said to Gao Jiong, Li Xun, and the rest, "This is desperate—we must break them by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 」於是擊所觀者，大囂而走，轉相騰藉，聲如雷霆。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they struck the spectators; a great clamor arose as they fled; they trampled one another in turn; the sound was like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: " They then struck at the spectators, who fled with a great uproar, trampling one another until the noise was like thunder.

sentences.zh: 忻乃傳呼曰：「賊敗矣！

translations.literal: Xin then passed the word, crying: "The rebels are defeated!
translations.idiomatic: Xin then shouted through the ranks, "The rebels are beaten!

sentences.zh: 」眾軍複振，齊力急擊之，迥軍大敗。

translations.literal: " The masses of troops revived; with united strength they pressed the attack fiercely; Jiong’s army was thoroughly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: " The army took heart again, struck together with all their force, and Jiong’s troops were utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 及平鄴城，以功加上柱國，賜奴婢二百口，牛馬羊萬計。

translations.literal: When Ye City was pacified, for merit he was given Supreme Pillar of State, granted two hundred male and female slaves, and cattle, horses, and sheep numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye fell he was made Supreme Pillar of State for his merit, given two hundred slaves, and cattle, horses, and sheep beyond count.

sentences.zh: 高祖顧謂忻曰：「尉迥傾山東之眾，運百萬之師，公舉無遺策，戰無全陣，誠天下之英傑也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu turned and said to Xin: "Yuchi Jiong marshaled the masses of Shandong and moved an army of a million; you proposed strategies without omission and fought battles without leaving a formation intact—truly a hero of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Xin and said, "Yuchi Jiong threw all Shandong into the field with an army of a million; you left no stratagem unused and no enemy line unbroken—truly you are the hero of the age.

sentences.zh: 」進封英國公，增邑三千戶。

translations.literal: " He was advanced to Duke of the State of Ying and his fief was increased by three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: " He was advanced to Duke of Ying and his fief increased by three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 自是以後，每參帷幄，出入臥內，禪代之際，忻有力焉。

translations.literal: From this time forward he always took part in the command tent, entering and leaving the inner sleeping quarters; at the time of the abdication and succession, Xin had a powerful hand in it.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he took part in every council of war and moved freely in and out of the inner apartments; when the throne changed hands, Xin had been a driving force.

sentences.zh: 後拜右領軍大將軍，恩顧彌重。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guards Army; favor and regard grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made General-in-Chief of the Right Guards Army, and the emperor’s favor toward him only deepened.

sentences.zh: 忻妙解兵法，馭戎齊整，當時六軍有一善事，雖非忻所建，在下輒相謂曰：「此必英公法也。

translations.literal: Xin had a subtle mastery of military law and governed troops in perfect order; whenever the six armies had some good practice, even if Xin had not established it, those below would say to one another: "This must be the Duke of Ying’s method.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had a master’s grasp of military doctrine and kept his troops in perfect order; whenever the six armies adopted some good practice, even if Xin had not devised it, the men below would say to one another, "That must be the Duke of Ying’s way.

sentences.zh: 」其見推服如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 後改封國公。

translations.literal: Later his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was changed to Duke of the State.

sentences.zh: 上嘗欲令忻率兵擊突厥，高熲言於上曰：「忻有異志，不可委以大兵。

translations.literal: The emperor once wished to have Xin lead troops against the Turks; Gao Jiong said to the emperor: "Xin harbors a different intent and cannot be entrusted with a great army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once meant to send Xin against the Turks, but Gao Jiong told him, "Xin has other ambitions and must not be given a great command.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " The plan was thereupon halted.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 忻既佐命功臣，頻經將領，有威名於當世。

translations.literal: Xin was already a founding merit-holder who had repeatedly served as commander and had a formidable reputation in his age.
translations.idiomatic: As a founding merit-holder who had repeatedly held high command, Xin enjoyed a formidable reputation in his day.

sentences.zh: 上由是微忌焉，以譴去官。

translations.literal: The emperor for this reason was slightly wary of him and removed him from office by reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore grew wary of him and dismissed him from office.

sentences.zh: 忻與梁士彥昵狎，數相往來，士彥時亦怨望，陰圖不軌。

translations.literal: Xin was intimate and familiar with Liang Shiyan; they frequently visited each other; Shiyan at that time also harbored resentment and secretly plotted irregular conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was on intimate terms with Liang Shiyan and they met often; Shiyan too nursed grievances and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 忻謂士彥曰：「帝王豈有常乎？

translations.literal: Xin said to Shiyan: "Are emperors and kings ever constant?
translations.idiomatic: Xin said to Shiyan, "Are emperors eternal?

sentences.zh: 相扶即是。

translations.literal: Mutual support is all that is needed.
translations.idiomatic: Men need only support one another.

sentences.zh: 公于蒲州起事，我必從征。

translations.literal: When you, sir, raise troops at Puzhou, I shall surely follow in the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When you rise at Puzhou, I shall march with you.

sentences.zh: 兩陣相當，然後連結，天下可圖也。

translations.literal: When the two armies face each other, then we join forces—the realm can be taken in hand.
translations.idiomatic: When our two armies stand face to face, we shall join forces and the realm may be ours.

sentences.zh: 」謀泄伏誅，年六十四，家口籍沒。

translations.literal: " The plot was exposed; he confessed and was executed; he was sixty-four years old; his household was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: " The plot was exposed; he confessed and was executed at sixty-four, and his entire household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 忻兄善，弘厚有武藝。

translations.literal: Xin’s elder brother Shan was magnanimous and possessed martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: Xin’s elder brother Shan was generous and skilled in arms.

sentences.zh: 仕周，官至上柱國、許國公。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, his office reached Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of the State of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he rose to Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，遇之甚厚，拜其子穎為上儀同。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he treated him very generously and appointed his son Ying as Supreme Yitong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne he treated Shan with great favor and made his son Ying Supreme Yitong.

sentences.zh: 及忻誅，並廢於家。

translations.literal: When Xin was executed, they were all reduced to commoners at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin was executed, they were all stripped of rank and confined at home.

sentences.zh: 善未幾卒。

translations.literal: Shan died before long.
translations.idiomatic: Shan died soon after.

sentences.zh: 穎至大業中為司農少卿。

translations.literal: Ying reached the post of Vice Minister of the Imperial Granaries in the Daye era.
translations.idiomatic: Ying rose to Vice Minister of the Imperial Granaries under Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 及李密逼東都，叛歸於密。

translations.literal: When Li Mi pressed the Eastern Capital, he rebelled and went over to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi threatened the Eastern Capital, he defected to Mi’s side.

sentences.zh: 忻弟愷，別有傳。

translations.literal: Xin’s younger brother Kai has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xin’s younger brother Kai is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 王誼王誼，字宜君，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yi—Wang Yi, styled Yijun, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, styled Yijun, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父顯，周鳳州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xian was Governor of Fengzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian had been governor of Fengzhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 誼少慷慨，有大志，便弓馬，博覽群言。

translations.literal: Yi in youth was generous and high-spirited, with great ambition; he was skilled in bow and horse and read widely among many writings.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yi was bold and high-minded, skilled in bow and horse, and widely read.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝時，為左中侍上士。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Min of Zhou, he was Senior Attendant of the Left Central Service.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Min of Zhou he served as Senior Attendant of the Left Central Service.

sentences.zh: 時大塚宰宇文護執政，勢傾王室，帝拱默無所關預。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Preceptor Yu Wenhu held power; his momentum overawed the royal house; the emperor bowed in silence and had no part in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Preceptor Yu Wenhu held real power and overshadowed the throne; the young emperor sat silent and had no voice in affairs.

sentences.zh: 有朝士於帝側微為不恭，誼勃然而進，將擊之。

translations.literal: A court gentleman at the emperor’s side was slightly disrespectful; Yi advanced with sudden anger and was about to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: When a courtier showed slight disrespect beside the emperor, Yi stepped forward in a rage to strike him.

sentences.zh: 其人惶懼請罪，乃止。

translations.literal: The man, fearful and alarmed, begged forgiveness, and Yi stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The man begged forgiveness in terror, and Yi desisted.

sentences.zh: 自是朝士無敢不肅。

translations.literal: From this time forward no court gentleman dared fail to be reverent.
translations.idiomatic: After that no courtier dared show disrespect in the emperor’s presence.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷禦正大夫。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Grand Master of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted to Grand Master of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，毀瘁過禮，廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: He encountered the hardship of his father’s death; his grief and emaciation exceeded the rites; he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to form the mound.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died his mourning exceeded the rites; he lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound himself.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起拜雍州別駕，固讓，不許。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned and appointed Vice Governor of Yongzhou; he firmly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was recalled and made Vice Governor of Yongzhou; he declined firmly but was not allowed to refuse.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，授儀同，累遷內史大夫，封楊國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu acceded, he was granted Yitong, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, and was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu came to the throne, Yi was made Yitong, rose through the ranks to Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, and was created Duke of Yang.

sentences.zh: 從帝伐齊，至并州，帝既入城，反為齊人所敗，左右多死。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor in the campaign against Qi; reaching Bingzhou, after the emperor had entered the city, he was in turn defeated by the men of Qi; many of those at the emperor’s side died.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor against Qi; at Bingzhou, after the emperor had entered the city, the Qi turned the tables and many of his escort were killed.

sentences.zh: 誼率麾下驍雄赴之，帝賴以全濟。

translations.literal: Yi led his valiant champions to rush to his aid; the emperor relied on this to escape whole.
translations.idiomatic: Yi led his bravest men to the rescue, and the emperor owed his survival to him.

sentences.zh: 時帝以六軍挫衄，將班師。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor, because the six armies had suffered setbacks, intended to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing the six armies beaten back, meant to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 誼固諫，帝從之。

translations.literal: Yi firmly remonstrated; the emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yi urged him firmly to press on, and the emperor took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及齊平，授相州刺史。

translations.literal: When Qi was pacified, he was appointed Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he was made governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複征為大內史。

translations.literal: Before long he was again summoned to be Grand Internal Historian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to serve as Grand Internal Historian.

sentences.zh: 汾州稽胡為亂，誼率兵擊之。

translations.literal: The Jiahu of Fenzhou rebelled; Yi led troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiahu of Fenzhou rose in rebellion, Yi led troops against them.

sentences.zh: 帝弟越王盛、譙王儉雖為總管，並受誼節度。

translations.literal: The emperor’s younger brothers, Prince Sheng of Yue and Prince Jian of Qiao, though they were commanders-in-chief, all received Yi’s direction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s brothers, Princes Sheng of Yue and Jian of Qiao, though supreme commanders themselves, were placed under Yi’s command.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the weight in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 及平賊而還，賜物五千段，封一子開國公。

translations.literal: When he had pacified the rebels and returned, he was granted five thousand lengths of goods and one son was enfeoffed as Duke with a founding fief.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were crushed and he returned, he received five thousand lengths of goods and one son was created a founding duke.

sentences.zh: 帝臨崩，謂皇太子曰：「王誼社稷臣，宜處以機密，不須遠任也。

translations.literal: As the emperor approached death, he said to the Crown Prince: "Wang Yi is a pillar of the state; he should be placed in confidential posts and need not be sent to distant appointments.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed the emperor told the crown prince, "Wang Yi is a pillar of the state; keep him close in confidential posts and do not send him far away.

sentences.zh: 皇太子即位，是為宣帝。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince acceded; this was Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince succeeded him as Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 憚誼剛正，出為襄州總管。

translations.literal: Fearing Yi’s firm uprightness, he sent him out as Commander-in-Chief of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yi’s blunt integrity, the new emperor sent him out as supreme commander of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，轉為鄭州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu became Chancellor, Yi was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became chancellor, Yi was transferred to supreme commander of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 司馬消難舉兵反，高祖以誼為行軍元帥，率四總管討之。

translations.literal: Sima Xiaonan raised troops in rebellion; Emperor Gaozu made Yi Campaign Marshal and led four commanders-in-chief to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiaonan rebelled, Yang Jian made Yi campaign marshal at the head of four supreme commanders to crush him.

sentences.zh: 軍次近郊，消難懼而奔陳。

translations.literal: When the army halted near the capital, Xiaonan, in fear, fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the suburbs, Xiaonan fled in fear to Chen.

sentences.zh: 于時北至商洛，南拒江淮，東西二千余裡，巴蠻多叛，共推渠帥蘭雒州為主。

translations.literal: At that time from the north to Shangluo and the south resisting the Jianghuai, east and west more than two thousand li, many of the Ba tribes rebelled and jointly made the chieftain Lan Luozhou their leader.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, from Shangluo in the north to the Huai and Yangtze in the south—a span of more than two thousand li—many Ba tribes rebelled and made the chieftain Lan Luozhou their leader.

sentences.zh: 雒州自號河南王，以附消難，北連尉迥。

translations.literal: Luozhou styled himself King of Henan, attached himself to Xiaonan, and linked with Yuchi Jiong in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou styled himself King of Henan, joined Xiaonan, and in the north linked arms with Yuchi Jiong.

sentences.zh: 誼率行軍總管李威、馮暉、李遠等分討之，旬月皆平。

translations.literal: Yi led the Campaign Commanders-in-Chief Li Wei, Feng Hui, Li Yuan, and others in separate suppressions; within a month all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent campaign commanders Li Wei, Feng Hui, Li Yuan, and others against them in separate columns, and within a month all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 高祖以誼前代舊臣，甚加禮敬，遣使勞問，冠蓋不絕。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because Yi was an old minister of the previous dynasty, treated him with great courtesy and respect, sending envoys to comfort and inquire after him; official carriages and caps never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yi was a veteran of the previous dynasty, Yang Jian treated him with exceptional courtesy; envoys bearing condolences and inquiries never ceased.

sentences.zh: 以第五女妻其子奉孝，尋拜大司徒。

translations.literal: He gave his fifth daughter in marriage to Yi’s son Fengxiao; shortly thereafter Yi was appointed Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his fifth daughter to Yi’s son Fengxiao in marriage and soon after appointed Yi Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 誼自以與高祖有舊，亦歸心焉。

translations.literal: Yi, considering himself to have old ties with Emperor Gaozu, also gave his heart to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, counting on his long friendship with Yang Jian, gave him his loyalty in return.

sentences.zh: 及上受禪，顧遇彌厚，上親幸其第，與之極歡。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, regard and treatment grew ever richer; the emperor personally visited his residence and shared the utmost joy with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne his favor toward Yi only deepened; the emperor visited his home in person and they feasted together in the greatest intimacy.

sentences.zh: 太常卿蘇威立議，以為戶口滋多，民田不贍，欲減功臣之地以給民。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Su Wei proposed a policy, holding that as registered households grew numerous, the people’s fields could not support them, and wishing to reduce the lands of merit-holders to give to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Su Wei proposed that as the population grew, farmland was insufficient and the lands of merit-holders should be reduced to provide for commoners.

sentences.zh: 誼奏曰：「百官者，曆世勳賢，方蒙爵土，一旦削之，未見其可。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized, saying: "The hundred officials are meritorious worthies of successive ages who have just received fiefs and lands; to cut them off at once—I do not see how that can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yi memorialized, "The officials are meritorious servants of successive reigns who have only just received fiefs; to strip them away at once—I see no good in that.

sentences.zh: 如臣所慮，正恐朝臣功德不建，何患人田有不足？

translations.literal: As this servant considers it, one should fear only that the court ministers’ merit is not established—why worry that the people’s fields are insufficient?
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, the real worry is that court ministers will lack incentive to build merit—why fret that the people lack land?

sentences.zh: 」上然之，竟寢威議。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved this and in the end shelved Wei’s proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and in the end set Wei’s proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，上將幸岐州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, the emperor was about to visit Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign the emperor planned a visit to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 誼諫曰：「陛下初臨萬國，人情未洽，何用此行？

translations.literal: Yi remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty has just come to the myriad states; popular sentiment is not yet harmonious—what need is there for this journey?
translations.idiomatic: Yi urged him, "Your Majesty has only just taken the throne; the people are not yet settled—why make this journey?

sentences.zh: 」上戲之曰：「吾昔與公位望齊等，一朝屈節為臣，或當恥愧。

translations.literal: " The emperor jested with him, saying: "In the past I and you, sir, were equal in rank and standing; in a single morning I bent my station to become your minister—perhaps there is shame.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor jested, "Once you and I stood as equals; now I have bent my station to become your sovereign—perhaps that shames you.

sentences.zh: 是行也，震揚威武，欲以服公心耳。

translations.literal: This journey is to display martial might and awe, wishing thereby to win your heart, sir.
translations.idiomatic: This journey is to display my martial majesty and win back your heart.

sentences.zh: 」誼笑而退。

translations.literal: " Yi smiled and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi smiled and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋奉使突厥，上嘉其稱旨，進封郢國公。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was sent on mission to the Turks; the emperor praised his accord with the imperial intent and advanced him to Duke of the State of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was sent on embassy to the Turks; the emperor praised his success and advanced him to Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其子奉孝卒。

translations.literal: Before long his son Fengxiao died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his son Fengxiao died.

sentences.zh: 逾年，誼上表，言公主少，請除服。

translations.literal: After a year Yi submitted a memorial, saying the princess was young and requesting removal of mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Yi submitted a memorial saying the princess was young and asking that mourning be ended.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫楊素劾誼曰：「臣聞喪服有五，親疏異節，喪制有四，降殺殊文。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yang Su impeached Yi, saying: "Your servant has heard that mourning garments have five grades with differing observances for near and distant kin, and mourning regulations have four types with differing texts for reduction and diminution.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yang Su impeached Yi, saying, "I have heard that mourning garments fall into five grades with differing observances for near and distant kin, and mourning regulations into four types with differing rules of reduction.

sentences.zh: 王者之所常行，故曰不易之道也。

translations.literal: These are what kings and lords constantly practice; therefore they are called the unchanging Way.
translations.idiomatic: These are what rulers constantly observe and are therefore called the unchanging Way.

sentences.zh: 是以賢者不得逾，不肖者不得不及。

translations.literal: Thus the worthy cannot exceed them, and the unworthy cannot fail to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the worthy may not exceed them and the unworthy may not fall short of them.

sentences.zh: 而儀同王奉孝既尚蘭陵公主，奉孝以去年五月身喪，始經一周，而誼便請除釋。

translations.literal: Yet the Yitong Wang Fengxiao had already married the Princess of Lanling; Fengxiao suffered the death of his person last year in the fifth month; it has only just completed one cycle, yet Yi immediately requested removal of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Yitong Wang Fengxiao had married the Princess of Lanling; Fengxiao died last May, and only one year has passed when Yi asks to end mourning.

sentences.zh: 竊以雖曰王姬，終成下嫁之禮，公則主之，猶在移天之義。

translations.literal: I venture to consider that though she is called a king’s daughter, in the end she completes the rites of marrying down; the duke as her father-in-law presides, and the meaning of shifting heaven still applies.
translations.idiomatic: Though she is called a king’s daughter, in the end she married down; as her father-in-law, the duke still stands in the relation of one who has received her from heaven.

sentences.zh: 況複三年之喪，自上達下，及期釋服，在禮未詳。

translations.literal: Moreover, the three-year mourning reaches from above to below; to release mourning garments when the period is reached is not clearly set forth in the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the three-year mourning runs from sovereign to subject; to end mourning when the period expires is nowhere clearly set forth in the rites.

sentences.zh: 然夫婦則人倫攸始，喪紀則人道至大，苟不重之，取笑君子。

translations.literal: Yet husband and wife are where human relations begin; mourning regulations are the greatest of human conduct—if one does not weight them heavily, one invites the ridicule of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet husband and wife are where human relations begin, and mourning is the greatest of human duties—if these are not honored, gentlemen will laugh.

sentences.zh: 故鑽燧改火，責以居喪之速；

translations.literal: Therefore when Zuan Sui changed the fire, he was blamed for the speed of his dwelling in mourning;
translations.idiomatic: Zuan Sui was rebuked for changing the fire too soon in his mourning;

sentences.zh: 朝祥暮歌，譏以忘哀之早。

translations.literal: morning auspices and evening songs brought ridicule for forgetting grief too early.
translations.idiomatic: and the man who sang at dusk after morning rites was mocked for forgetting grief too soon.

sentences.zh: 然誼雖不自強，爵位已重，欲為無禮，其可得乎？

translations.literal: Yet though Yi does not force himself, his rank and position are already weighty; if he wishes to be without rites, how can that be permitted?
translations.idiomatic: Yi may not force the issue, but his rank is already exalted; if he wishes to cast off ritual, how can that be allowed?

sentences.zh: 乃薄俗傷教，為父則不慈；

translations.literal: This is shallow custom that injures teaching—as a father he is not compassionate;
translations.idiomatic: This is shallow custom that injures teaching—as a father he shows no compassion;

sentences.zh: 輕禮易喪，致婦於無義。

translations.literal: he treats rites lightly and changes mourning easily, bringing the woman into a state without righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: he treats ritual lightly and hurries mourning, leaving his daughter-in-law without righteousness.

sentences.zh: 若縱而不正，恐傷風俗，請付法推科。

translations.literal: If he is indulged and not corrected, I fear custom and mores will be injured; I request that he be handed over to the law for prosecution according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: If this is indulged and not corrected, custom and mores will suffer; I ask that he be handed over to the law for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 」有詔勿治，然恩禮稍薄。

translations.literal: " An edict was issued not to prosecute, but favor and courtesy grew somewhat thin.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered that he not be prosecuted, but the emperor’s favor toward him cooled.

sentences.zh: 誼頗怨望。

translations.literal: Yi harbored considerable resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yi nursed considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 或告誼謀反，上令案其事。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Yi plotted rebellion; the emperor ordered an investigation of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Yi was plotting rebellion, and the emperor ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 主者奏誼有不遜之言，實無反狀。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported that Yi had disrespectful words but in truth there was no sign of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The investigators reported disrespectful words but no actual sign of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上賜酒而釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted him wine and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him wine and released him.

sentences.zh: 于時上柱國元諧亦頗失意，誼數與相往來，言論醜惡。

translations.literal: At that time the Supreme Pillar of State Yuan Xie was also quite discontent; Yi frequently visited back and forth with him, and their talk was ugly and vile.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Supreme Pillar of State Yuan Xie was also deeply discontented; Yi met with him often and their talk was ugly and seditious.

sentences.zh: 胡僧告之，公卿奏誼大逆不道，罪當死。

translations.literal: A barbarian monk reported them; the nobles and ministers memorialized that Yi had committed the greatest impiety and disloyalty and his crime deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk informed on them; the nobles memorialized that Yi had committed treason and deserved death.

sentences.zh: 上見誼，愴然曰：「朕與公舊為同學，甚相憐湣，將奈國法何？

translations.literal: The emperor saw Yi and said mournfully: "I and you, sir, were once schoolmates; I pity you deeply—what can I do about the laws of the state?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw Yi he said mournfully, "You and I were schoolmates once; I pity you deeply—what can I do against the law of the land?

sentences.zh: 」於是下詔曰：「誼，有周之世，早豫人倫，朕共遊庠序，遂相親好。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he issued an edict, saying: "Yi, in the age of Zhou, early entered human relations; I studied with him in the school and we became close friends.
translations.idiomatic: " He then issued an edict: "Yi, in the Zhou era, early took his place among men; I studied with him and we became close friends.

sentences.zh: 然性懷險薄，巫覡盈門，鬼言怪語，稱神道聖。

translations.literal: Yet his nature harbored peril and shallowness; shamans and wizards filled his gates; ghostly words and strange speech called him the sage of the divine Way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was treacherous and shallow; shamans filled his gates with ghostly words and strange speech, calling him a sage of the divine Way.

sentences.zh: 朕受命之初，深存誡約，口雲改悔，心實不悛。

translations.literal: At the beginning when I received the Mandate, I deeply set forth admonitions and covenants; his mouth said he would reform and repent, but his heart in truth did not change.
translations.idiomatic: When I first received the Mandate I warned him deeply; his mouth promised repentance but his heart never changed.

sentences.zh: 乃說四天正神道，誼應受命，書有誼讖，天有誼星，桃、鹿二川，岐州之下，歲在辰巳，興帝王之業。

translations.literal: He then preached the divine Way of the Four Heavenly Correctors, that Yi should receive the Mandate; writings contained prophecies of Yi; heaven had the star of Yi; the two rivers Tao and Lu, below Qizhou—in the years of chen and si—he would raise the enterprise of emperor and king.
translations.idiomatic: He preached the divine Way of the Four Heavenly Correctors, saying Yi was destined to receive the Mandate; books held prophecies of Yi, heaven held the star of Yi; below Qizhou, where the Tao and Lu rivers meet, in the years of chen and si, he would raise an imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 密令卜問，伺殿省之災。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered divination and inquiry, watching for disasters in the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered divinations, watching for disaster in the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 又說其身是明王，信用左道，所在詿誤，自言相表，當王不疑。

translations.literal: He also said that his person was a Bright King, trusted heterodox ways, everywhere misled and deceived, and declared of his own physiognomy that he should be king without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: He also claimed to be a Bright King, trusted heterodox cults, misled people wherever he went, and insisted that his physiognomy showed he was destined to rule without question.

sentences.zh: 此而赦之，將或為亂，禁暴除惡，宜伏國刑。

translations.literal: If this man is pardoned, he may yet make rebellion; to restrain violence and remove evil, he should submit to the laws of the state.
translations.idiomatic: If he is pardoned he may yet stir rebellion; to restrain violence and root out evil, he should suffer the penalty of the state.

sentences.zh: 」上複令大理正趙綽謂誼曰：「時命如此，將若之何！

translations.literal: " The emperor again ordered Director of the Court of Review Zhao Chuo to say to Yi: "Fate is thus—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then had Director of the Court of Review Zhao Chuo tell Yi, "Fate has brought us to this—what can be done!

sentences.zh: 」於是賜死于家，時年四十六。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was granted death at home; he was forty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then granted death at home at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 元諧元諧，河南洛陽人也，家代貴盛。

translations.literal: Yuan Xie—Yuan Xie was a man of Luoyang in Henan; his family had been noble and prosperous for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xie came from Luoyang in Henan; his family had been noble and prosperous for generations.

sentences.zh: 諧性豪俠，有氣調。

translations.literal: Xie’s nature was bold and chivalrous; he had spirit and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was bold and chivalrous by nature, with spirit and presence.

sentences.zh: 少與高祖同受業于國子，甚相友愛。

translations.literal: In youth he studied together with Emperor Gaozu at the Imperial Academy and they were very friendly and affectionate.
translations.idiomatic: As youths he and Yang Jian studied together at the Imperial Academy and were close friends.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功，累遷大將軍。

translations.literal: Later, on account of military merit, he was repeatedly promoted to Great General.
translations.idiomatic: Later, through military merit, he rose to Great General.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，引致左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu became Chancellor, he was brought in to attend at his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became chancellor, he brought Xie into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 諧白高祖曰：「公無黨援，譬如水間一堵牆，大危矣。

translations.literal: Xie informed Emperor Gaozu, saying: "Your Grace has no factional support—like a single wall amid water, you are in great peril.
translations.idiomatic: Xie told Yang Jian, "You have no factional backing—you are like a lone wall in midstream, in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 公其勉之。

translations.literal: Your Grace must exert yourself.
translations.idiomatic: You must press on with all your strength.

sentences.zh: 」尉迥作亂，遣兵寇小鄉，令諧擊破之。

translations.literal: " When Yuchi Jiong made rebellion, he sent troops to raid Xiaoxiang; he ordered Xie to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yuchi Jiong rebelled and sent troops against Xiaoxiang, Yang Jian ordered Xie to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，上顧諧笑曰：「水間牆竟何如也？

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, the emperor turned to Xie and smiled, saying: "How did that wall amid water turn out after all?
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne he turned to Xie and smiled, "How did that wall in midstream fare?

sentences.zh: 」於是賜宴極歡。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he granted a feast of the utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave a feast of the greatest intimacy.

sentences.zh: 進位上大將軍，封樂安郡公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Supreme Great General, enfeoffed as Duke of Le’an Commandery with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supreme Great General and created Duke of Le’an with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 奉詔參修律令。

translations.literal: He received an edict to take part in revising statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take part in revising the law code.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾寇涼州，詔諧為行軍元帥，率行軍總管賀婁子幹、郭竣、元浩等步騎數萬擊之。

translations.literal: At that time Tuyuhun raided Liangzhou; an edict appointed Xie Campaign Marshal, leading the Campaign Commanders-in-Chief Helou Zigan, Guo Jun, Yuan Hao, and others with several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided Liangzhou, Xie was made campaign marshal at the head of several campaign commanders and tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 上敕諧曰：「公受朝寄，總兵西下，本欲自寧疆境，保全黎庶，非是貪無用之地，害荒服之民。

translations.literal: The emperor charged Xie, saying: "You, sir, have received the court’s trust and command troops westward; the original intent is to bring peace to the borders and preserve the common people—not to covet useless lands and harm the people of the wild frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed Xie, "You bear the court’s trust and command troops westward to bring peace to the frontier and preserve the people—not to seize useless land and harm the subjects of the wild borderlands.

sentences.zh: 王者之師，意在仁義。

translations.literal: The army of a king or lord aims at benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The army of a true king aims at benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 渾賊若至界首者，公宜曉示以德，臨之以教，誰敢不服也！

translations.literal: If the Tuyuhun bandits reach the border markers, you, sir, should enlighten them with virtue and face them with teaching—who would dare not submit!
translations.idiomatic: If the Tuyuhun reach the border, enlighten them with virtue and face them with teaching—who would dare refuse to submit!

sentences.zh: 」時賊將定城王鐘利房率騎三千渡河，連結党項。

translations.literal: " At that time the rebel general the Prince of Dingcheng, Zhong Lifang, led three thousand horsemen across the river and linked with the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the rebel general Prince Zhong Lifang of Dingcheng led three thousand horsemen across the river and allied with the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 諧率兵出鄯州，趣青海，邀其歸路。

translations.literal: Xie led troops out from Shanzhou, hastened toward Qinghai, and intercepted their line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Xie marched from Shanzhou toward Qinghai to cut off their retreat.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾引兵拒諧，相遇于豐利山。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun brought troops to resist Xie; they met at Fengli Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun brought troops to meet him at Fengli Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊鐵騎二萬，與諧大戰，諧擊走之。

translations.literal: The enemy’s iron cavalry numbered twenty thousand; they fought a great battle with Xie; Xie attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand enemy iron cavalry fought a great battle with Xie, and he drove them off.

sentences.zh: 賊駐兵青海，遣其太子可博汗以勁騎五萬來掩官軍。

translations.literal: The enemy encamped at Qinghai and sent their crown prince Kebohan with fifty thousand picked horsemen to surprise the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy encamped at Qinghai and sent Crown Prince Kebohan with fifty thousand picked horsemen to fall on the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 諧逆擊，敗之，追奔三十餘裡，俘斬萬計，虜大震駭。

translations.literal: Xie met them in counterattack, defeated them, pursued in flight for more than thirty li, captured and killed numbering in the tens of thousands; the barbarians were greatly shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Xie met them head-on, routed them, and pursued more than thirty li, capturing and killing beyond count; the barbarians were utterly terrified.

sentences.zh: 於是移書諭以禍福，其名王十七人、公侯十三人各率其所部來降。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent a letter explaining fortune and calamity; seventeen titled kings and thirteen dukes and marquises each led their own followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent letters explaining fortune and calamity, and seventeen titled kings and thirteen dukes and marquises led their followers to submit.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，下詔曰：「褒善疇庸，有聞前載，諧識用明達，神情警悟，文規武略，譽流朝野。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and issued an edict, saying: "To reward goodness and rank merit has been heard of in former records; Xie’s knowledge and employment are bright and penetrating, his spirit and expression alert and keen; his literary rules and military strategies—his fame flows through court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and issued an edict: "To reward merit is an ancient practice; Xie is bright and penetrating in counsel, alert in spirit, renowned in court and countryside for his civil and military gifts.

sentences.zh: 申威拓土，功成疆埸，深謀大節，實簡朕心。

translations.literal: He displayed might and extended territory; merit was achieved at the borders; deep strategy and great integrity truly winnow my heart.
translations.idiomatic: He displayed might abroad and extended the borders; his deep strategy and great integrity have truly won my heart.

sentences.zh: 加禮延代，宜隆賞典。

translations.literal: Increase his honors to extend through generations; he should receive lofty rewards according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Let his honors extend through generations and let his rewards be fittingly great.

sentences.zh: 可柱國，別封一子縣公。

translations.literal: He may be made Pillar of State; one son separately enfeoffed as Duke of a county.
translations.idiomatic: He is to be made Pillar of State, and one son separately created a county duke.

sentences.zh: 」諧拜甯州刺史，頗有威惠。

translations.literal: " Xie was appointed Governor of Ningzhou and had considerable authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie was appointed governor of Ningzhou and governed with both authority and kindness.

sentences.zh: 然剛愎，好排詆，不能取媚於左右。

translations.literal: Yet he was stubborn and willful, fond of slandering others, and could not win favor with those at the emperor’s side.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stubborn and fond of slander, and could not win favor with those around the throne.

sentences.zh: 嘗言於上曰：「臣一心事主，不曲取人意。

translations.literal: He once said to the emperor: "Your servant serves the lord with one heart and does not bend to win others’ approval.
translations.idiomatic: He once told the emperor, "I serve Your Majesty with a single heart and will not bend to win others’ approval.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「宜終此言。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "You should hold to this saying to the end.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Hold to that to the end.

sentences.zh: 」後以公事免。

translations.literal: " Later he was dismissed on account of public business.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he was dismissed for an official offense.

sentences.zh: 時上柱國王誼有功于國，與諧俱無任用，每相往來。

translations.literal: At that time the Supreme Pillar of State Wang Yi had merit for the state; he and Xie were both without employment and frequently visited each other.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Supreme Pillar of State Wang Yi, who had served the state with merit, and Xie were both without office and met often.

sentences.zh: 胡僧告諧、誼謀反，上按其事，無逆狀，上慰諭而釋之。

translations.literal: A barbarian monk reported that Xie and Yi plotted rebellion; the emperor investigated the matter; there was no sign of treason; the emperor comforted and instructed them and released them.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk reported that Xie and Yi were plotting rebellion; the emperor investigated and found no treason; he comforted them and released them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，誼伏誅，諧漸被疏忌。

translations.literal: Before long Yi confessed and was executed; Xie was gradually treated with distance and suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yi was executed; Xie was gradually distrusted.

sentences.zh: 然以龍潛之舊，每預朝請，恩禮無虧。

translations.literal: Yet because of old ties from the time of hidden dragon, he always took part in court audiences; favor and courtesy were not diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because of their old ties from before Yang Jian took the throne, he still attended court and received undiminished courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及上大宴百僚，諧進曰：「陛下威德遠被，臣請突厥可汗為候正，陳叔寶為令史。

translations.literal: When the emperor gave a great feast to the hundred officials, Xie advanced and said: "Your Majesty’s might and virtue extend far; your servant requests the Turk qaghan as lookout officer and Chen Shubao as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At a great feast for the officials, Xie proposed, "Your Majesty’s might reaches far abroad; I ask that the Turk qaghan serve as lookout officer and Chen Shubao as clerk.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕平陳國，以伐罪吊人，非欲誇誕取威天下。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I pacified the state of Chen to punish crime and comfort the people—not to boast and take awe over the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I conquered Chen to punish wrongdoing and comfort the people—not to boast and awe the world.

sentences.zh: 公之所奏，殊非朕心。

translations.literal: What you, sir, have memorialized is utterly not my heart.
translations.idiomatic: What you propose is far from my intent.

sentences.zh: 突厥不知山川，何能警候！

translations.literal: The Turks do not know mountains and rivers—how can they keep watch!
translations.idiomatic: The Turks know nothing of our mountains and rivers—how could they keep watch!

sentences.zh: 叔寶昏醉，寧堪驅使！

translations.literal: Shubao is muddled and drunk—how could he be fit to be driven!
translations.idiomatic: Shubao is a drunken fool—how could he be put to use!

sentences.zh: 」諧默然而退。

translations.literal: " Xie fell silent and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie fell silent and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，有人告諧與從父弟上開府滂、臨澤侯田鸞、上儀同祁緒等謀反。

translations.literal: Several years later someone reported that Xie, together with his paternal cousin the Shang Kaifu Pang, the Marquis of Linze Tian Luan, the Supreme Yitong Qi Xu, and others plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later someone reported that Xie, with his cousin Pang, Marquis Tian Luan of Linze, Supreme Yitong Qi Xu, and others, was plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上令案其事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered an investigation of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「諧謀令祁緒勒党項兵，即斷巴蜀。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported: "Xie plotted to have Qi Xu drive Tangut troops and immediately cut off Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The investigators reported that Xie planned to have Qi Xu lead Tangut troops to cut off Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 時廣平王雄、左僕射高熲二人用事，諧欲譖去之，雲：'左執法星動已四年矣，狀一奏，高熲必死。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Xiong of Guangping and Left Vice Director Gao Jiong were the two in power; Xie wished to slander and remove them, saying: 'The Left Law-Enforcer star has been in motion for four years already; with one memorial submitted, Gao Jiong is sure to die.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiong of Guangping and Left Vice Director Gao Jiong then held power; Xie wished to destroy them, saying, "The Left Law-Enforcer star has been in motion four years; one memorial and Gao Jiong is dead.

sentences.zh: '又言：'太白犯月，光芒相照，主殺大臣，楊雄必當之。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'The Great White invades the moon; their radiances shine on each other—it presages the killing of a great minister; Yang Xiong is sure to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The Great White star invades the moon, their radiances meet—it presages the death of a great minister, and Yang Xiong will be the one.

sentences.zh: '諧嘗與滂同謁上，諧私謂滂曰：'我是主人，殿上者賊也。

translations.literal: ' Xie once attended audience with Pang; Xie privately said to Pang: 'I am the host; those on the dais are bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Xie and Pang attended court together, Xie whispered to Pang, "I am the true host; those on the throne are thieves.

sentences.zh: '因令滂望氣，滂曰：'彼雲似蹲狗走鹿，不如我輩有福德雲。

translations.literal: ' He then had Pang observe the qi of the clouds; Pang said: 'Their clouds are like crouching dogs and running deer—not equal to our clouds of fortune and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He had Pang read the clouds; Pang said, "Their clouds look like crouching dogs and running deer—not like our clouds of fortune and virtue.

sentences.zh: '」上大怒，諧、滂、鸞、緒並伏誅，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: '" The emperor was greatly enraged; Xie, Pang, Luan, and Xu all confessed and were executed; their households were registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was furious; Xie, Pang, Luan, and Xu were all executed and their households confiscated.

sentences.zh: 王世積王世積，闡熙新渼人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shiji—Wang Shiji was a man of Xinmei in Zhanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiji came from Xinmei in Zhanxi.

sentences.zh: 父雅，周使持節、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His father Ya was Zhou’s Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Kaifu Yitong Sanqi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ya had been Zhou’s Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Kaifu Yitong Sanqi.

sentences.zh: 世積容貌魁岸，腰帶十圍，風神爽拔，有傑人之表。

translations.literal: Shiji’s appearance was towering; his waist belt was ten wei in girth; his spirit and bearing were bright and outstanding; he had the bearing of a hero among men.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was towering in stature, his waist ten hands around, spirited and outstanding, with the bearing of a born champion.

sentences.zh: 在周有軍功，拜上儀同，封長子縣公。

translations.literal: Under Zhou he had military merit, was appointed Supreme Yitong, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changzi County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he won military merit, was made Supreme Yitong, and created Duke of Changzi.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂，從韋孝寬擊之，每戰有功，拜上大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, Yuchi Jiong made rebellion; he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him; in every battle he had merit and was appointed Supreme Great General.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chancellor and Yuchi Jiong rebelled, he followed Wei Xiaokuan, won merit in every battle, and was made Supreme Great General.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進封宜陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was advanced to Duke of Yiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Shiji was advanced to Duke of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 高熲美其才能，甚善之。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong praised his talent and ability and was very fond of him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong admired his talent and was very fond of him.

sentences.zh: 嘗密謂熲曰：「吾輩俱周之臣子，社稷淪滅，其若之何？

translations.literal: He once secretly said to Jiong: "We are all subjects and sons of Zhou; the altars of soil and grain have fallen and perished—what is to be done?
