translations.idiomatic: He once said secretly to Jiong, "We are all servants of Zhou; the dynasty has fallen—what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 」熲深拒其言。

translations.literal: " Jiong deeply rejected his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiong firmly rejected his words.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授蘄州總管。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made supreme commander of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以舟師自蘄水趣九江，與陳將紀瑱戰於蘄口，大破之。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, with a naval force he hastened from the Qi River toward Jiujiang, fought the Chen general Ji Zhen at Qikou, and thoroughly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Chen he led a fleet from the Qi River toward Jiujiang, met the Chen general Ji Zhen at Qikou, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 既而晉王廣已平丹陽，世積於是移書告諭，遣千金公權始璋略取新蔡。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Prince Jin Guang had already pacified Danyang; Shiji thereupon sent letters of notification and persuasion, dispatching the Duke of a Thousand Gold Quan Shizhang to seize Xincai in a raid.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guang of Jin had taken Danyang, Shiji sent letters of surrender and dispatched Duke Quan Shizhang to seize Xincai.

sentences.zh: 陳江州司馬黃偲棄城而遁，始璋入據其城。

translations.literal: The Chen Jiangzhou Chief Administrator Huang Si abandoned the city and fled; Shizhang entered and occupied the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen chief administrator of Jiangzhou, Huang Si, abandoned the city and fled; Shizhang entered and held it.

sentences.zh: 世積繼至，陳豫章太守徐璒、廬陵太守蕭廉、潯陽太守陸仲容、巴山太守王誦、太原太守馬頲、齊昌太守黃正始、安成太守任瓘等，及鄱陽、臨川守將，並詣世積降。

translations.literal: When Shiji arrived in succession, the Chen governors Xu Qiong of Yuzhang, Xiao Lian of Luling, Lu Zhongrong of Xunyang, Wang Song of Bashan, Ma Ting of Taiyuan, Huang Zhengshi of Qichang, Ren Jin of Ancheng, and others, as well as the defending generals of Poyang and Linchuan, all came to Shiji to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiji arrived, the Chen governors of Yuzhang, Luling, Xunyang, Bashan, Taiyuan, Qichang, and Ancheng, and the garrison commanders of Poyang and Linchuan, all came to surrender to him.

sentences.zh: 以功進位柱國、荊州總管，賜絹五千段，加之寶帶，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Pillar of State and Commander-in-Chief of Jingzhou, granted five thousand lengths of silk, given in addition a precious belt, and a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Pillar of State and supreme commander of Jingzhou, given five thousand lengths of silk, a precious belt, and a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，桂州人李光仕作亂，世積以行軍總管討平之。

translations.literal: Several years later the man of Guizhou Li Guangshi made rebellion; Shiji as Campaign Commander-in-Chief suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Li Guangshi of Guizhou rebelled; Shiji crushed the revolt as campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 上遣都官員外郎辛凱卿馳勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the Vice Director of the Office of Capital Affairs Xin Kaiqing by relay horse to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Director of the Office of Capital Affairs Xin Kaiqing by relay horse to congratulate him.

sentences.zh: 及還，進位上柱國，賜物二千段。

translations.literal: When he returned, he was advanced to Supreme Pillar of State and granted two thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Supreme Pillar of State and given two thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 上甚重之。

translations.literal: The emperor valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 世積見上性忌刻，功臣多獲罪，由是縱酒，不與執政言及時事。

translations.literal: Shiji saw that the emperor’s nature was jealous and harsh and that merit-holders frequently incurred guilt; for this reason he gave himself to drink and did not speak with those in power about current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji saw that the emperor was jealous and harsh and that many merit-holders had been punished; he took to drink and would not discuss current affairs with those in power.

sentences.zh: 上以為有酒疾，舍之宮內，令醫者療之。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that he had an alcohol ailment, lodged him within the palace, and ordered physicians to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought he had a drinking sickness, kept him in the palace, and ordered physicians to treat him.

sentences.zh: 世積詭稱疾愈，始得就第。

translations.literal: Shiji falsely claimed his illness was cured and only then was permitted to go to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji pretended to be cured and was only then allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 及起遼東之役，世積與漢王並為行軍元帥，至柳城，遇疾疫而還。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Liaodong was launched, Shiji and the Prince of Han were both Campaign Marshals; reaching Liucheng, they encountered epidemic disease and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liaodong campaign began, Shiji and the Prince of Han served as campaign marshals; at Liucheng they met epidemic disease and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 拜涼州總管，令騎士七百人送之官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Liangzhou; seven hundred horsemen were ordered to escort him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supreme commander of Liangzhou, with seven hundred horsemen to escort him to his post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其親信安定皇甫孝諧有罪，吏捕之，亡抵世積。

translations.literal: Before long his trusted follower Huangfu Xiaoxie of Anding committed a crime; officials arrested him; he fled and reached Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his confidant Huangfu Xiaoxie of Anding committed a crime; when officers came to arrest him he fled to Shiji.

sentences.zh: 世積不納，由是有憾。

translations.literal: Shiji did not receive him; for this reason there was resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji refused to shelter him, and from that arose resentment.

sentences.zh: 孝諧竟配防桂州，事總管令狐熙。

translations.literal: Xiaoxie was in the end assigned to garrison defense at Guizhou and served Commander-in-Chief Linghu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxie was sent in the end to garrison Guizhou under Commander Linghu Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙又不之禮，甚困窮，因徼幸上變，稱：「世積嘗令道人相其貴不，道人答曰：'公當為國主。

translations.literal: Xi also did not treat him with courtesy; he was in extreme poverty and hardship; he therefore seized the chance to report a change to the throne, saying: "Shiji once had a Daoist priest read whether he would be noble; the priest answered: 'Your Grace should be lord of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Xi also treated him poorly, and in his poverty Xiaoxie seized the chance to inform the throne, saying, "Shiji once had a Daoist read his fortune; the priest said, 'You will be lord of the state.

sentences.zh: '謂其妻曰：'夫人當為皇后。

translations.literal: ' He told his wife: 'Madam should be empress.
translations.idiomatic: He told his wife, 'You will be empress.

sentences.zh: '又將之涼州，其所親謂世積曰：'河西天下精兵處，可以圖大事也。

translations.literal: ' Again, when he was about to go to Liangzhou, those close to him said to Shiji: 'Hexi is where the realm’s picked troops are; great affairs can be plotted there.
translations.idiomatic: When he was leaving for Liangzhou, his intimates told Shiji, 'Hexi holds the finest troops in the realm; there you may plot great affairs.

sentences.zh: '世積曰：'涼州土曠人稀，非用武之國。

translations.literal: ' Shiji said: 'Liangzhou’s land is broad and its people sparse—it is not a state for using arms.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji said, 'Liangzhou is broad and thinly peopled—not a land for raising armies.

sentences.zh: '」由是被征入朝，按其事。

translations.literal: '" Thereupon he was summoned to court and the matter was investigated.
translations.idiomatic: " He was summoned to court and the matter investigated.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「左衛大將軍元旻、右衛大將軍元胄、左僕射高熲，並與世積交通，受其名馬之贈。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported: "Left Guards General Yuan Min, Right Guards General Yuan Zhou, and Left Vice Director Gao Jiong all had dealings with Shiji and received famous horses as gifts from him.
translations.idiomatic: The investigators reported that Left Guards General Yuan Min, Right Guards General Yuan Zhou, and Left Vice Director Gao Jiong had all had dealings with Shiji and accepted famous horses from him.

sentences.zh: 」世積竟坐誅，旻、胄等免官，拜孝諧為上大將軍。

translations.literal: " Shiji in the end was implicated and executed; Min, Zhou, and the others were dismissed from office; Xiaoxie was appointed Supreme Great General.
translations.idiomatic: " Shiji was executed in the end; Min, Zhou, and the others were dismissed; Xiaoxie was made Supreme Great General.

sentences.zh: 虞慶則虞慶則，京兆櫟陽人也。

translations.literal: Yu Qingze—Yu Qingze was a man of Liyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qingze came from Liyang in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 本姓魚。

translations.literal: His original surname was Yu (Fish).
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Yu.

sentences.zh: 其先仕于赫連氏，遂家靈武，代為北邊豪傑。

translations.literal: His ancestors served the Helian clan and then made their home at Lingwu; for generations they were powerful figures of the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had served the Helian clan and settled at Lingwu; for generations they were powerful on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 父祥，周靈武太守。

translations.literal: His father Xiang was Governor of Lingwu under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang had been governor of Lingwu under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 慶則幼雄毅，性倜儻，身長八尺，有膽氣，善鮮卑語，身被重鎧，帶兩鞬，左右馳射，本州豪俠皆敬憚之。

translations.literal: Qingze in youth was fierce and resolute; his nature was unrestrained; his body was eight chi tall; he had courage and spirit; he was skilled in Xianbei speech; he wore heavy armor, carried two quivers, shot on horseback to left and right; the chivalrous heroes of his prefecture all respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Qingze was fierce and bold, eight feet tall, brave, fluent in Xianbei, able to wear heavy armor and shoot from horseback with quivers at either side; the frontier champions of his district all respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 初以弋獵為事，中便折節讀書，常慕傅介子、班仲升為人。

translations.literal: At first he took hunting with bow as his occupation; in mid-life he abruptly reformed himself to read books and constantly admired the persons of Fu Jiezi and Ban Zhongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: At first he lived by the hunt; in mid-life he turned to books and admired the careers of Fu Jiezi and Ban Chao.

sentences.zh: 仕周，釋褐中外府行參軍，稍遷外兵參軍事，襲爵沁源縣公。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he doffed his commoner’s garb as Attendant Staff Officer of the Central and Outer Offices, was gradually promoted to Staff Officer for External Military Affairs, and inherited the title Duke of Qinyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he began as staff officer of the central offices, rose to staff officer for external military affairs, and inherited the title Duke of Qinyuan.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，授儀同大將軍，除并州總管長史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was appointed Yitong Great General and made Chief Administrator to the Commander-in-Chief of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was made Yitong Great General and chief administrator to the commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，授開府。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Kaifu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Kaifu.

sentences.zh: 時稽胡數為反叛，越王盛、內史下大夫高熲討平之。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiahu frequently rebelled; Prince Sheng of Yue and the Lower Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat Gao Jiong suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiahu rebelled repeatedly, Prince Sheng of Yue and Lower Grand Master Gao Jiong pacified them.

sentences.zh: 將班師，熲與盛謀，須文武幹略者鎮遏之。

translations.literal: When they were about to withdraw the army, Jiong and Sheng plotted that they needed a man of civil and military capacity and strategy to hold the region down.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to withdraw, Jiong and Sheng agreed that a man of civil and military capacity was needed to hold the region down.

sentences.zh: 表請慶則，於是即拜石州總管。

translations.literal: They memorialized requesting Qingze; thereupon he was immediately appointed Commander-in-Chief of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized for Qingze, and he was immediately made supreme commander of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 甚有威惠，境內清肅，稽胡慕義而歸者八千餘戶。

translations.literal: He had considerable authority and kindness; within the borders all was clear and solemn; more than eight thousand households of Jiahu who admired righteousness returned to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with authority and kindness; the region was peaceful, and more than eight thousand Jiahu households came over in admiration of his rule.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，進位大將軍，遷內史監、吏部尚書、京兆尹，封彭城郡公，營新都總監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was advanced to Great General, transferred to Director of the Palace Secretariat, Minister of Personnel, Governor of Jingzhao, enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng Commandery, and made Supervisor of Construction for the New Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 1 he was promoted to Great General, made Director of the Palace Secretariat, Minister of Personnel, and Governor of Jingzhao, created Duke of Pengcheng, and put in charge of building the new capital.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，突厥入寇，慶則為元帥討之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year the Turks invaded; Qingze served as marshal to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year 2 the Turks invaded, and Qingze was made marshal to repel them.

sentences.zh: 部分失所，士卒多寒凍，墮指者千餘人。

translations.literal: The divisions lost their positions; many soldiers suffered cold and freezing; more than a thousand had frostbitten fingers drop off.
translations.idiomatic: The columns lost their way; many soldiers froze, and more than a thousand suffered frostbite so severe their fingers dropped off.

sentences.zh: 偏將達奚長儒率騎兵二千人別道邀賊，為虜所圍，甚急，慶則案營不救。

translations.literal: The flank general Daxi Changru led two thousand horsemen by a separate route to intercept the enemy, was surrounded by the barbarians in extreme peril, yet Qingze sat in camp and did not rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Flank general Daxi Changru led two thousand horsemen by another route to intercept the enemy, was surrounded in desperate straits, yet Qingze sat in camp and would not rescue him.

sentences.zh: 由是長儒孤軍獨戰，死者十八九。

translations.literal: For this reason Changru’s lone army fought alone; eight or nine out of ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Changru’s isolated force fought alone, and eight or nine out of ten were killed.

sentences.zh: 上不之責也。

translations.literal: The emperor did not blame him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not hold him accountable.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 後突厥主攝圖將內附，請一重臣充使，於是上遣慶則詣突厥所。

translations.literal: Later the Turk sovereign Shetu was about to submit inwardly and requested a weighty minister to serve as envoy; the emperor thereupon dispatched Qingze to the Turk encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Turk qaghan Shetu prepared to submit and asked for a senior minister as envoy; the emperor sent Qingze to the Turk camp.

sentences.zh: 攝圖恃強，初欲亢禮，慶則責以往事，攝圖不服。

translations.literal: Shetu relied on his strength and at first wished to treat him as an equal; Qingze reproached him with past affairs; Shetu would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu, counting on his strength, at first meant to receive him as an equal; Qingze rebuked him with past offenses, and Shetu refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 其介長孫晟又說諭之，攝圖及弟葉護皆拜受詔，因即稱臣朝貢，請永為籓附。

translations.literal: His aide Zhangsun Sheng again persuaded and instructed him; Shetu and his younger brother Yehu both bowed to receive the edict; thereupon they styled themselves subjects, sent tribute to court, and requested to be forever a frontier dependency.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Zhangsun Sheng persuaded him further; Shetu and his brother Yehu bowed to receive the edict, styled themselves subjects, sent tribute, and asked to remain a vassal forever.

sentences.zh: 初，慶則出使，高祖敕之曰：「我欲存立突厥，彼送公馬，但取五三匹。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qingze went on mission, Emperor Gaozu charged him, saying: "I wish to preserve and establish the Turks; if they present horses to you, sir, take only five or three.
translations.idiomatic: Before Qingze departed, the emperor instructed him, "I mean to preserve the Turks; if they offer you horses, take only a few.

sentences.zh: 」攝圖見慶則，贈馬千匹，又以女妻之。

translations.literal: " When Shetu saw Qingze he presented a thousand horses and also gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: " Shetu gave him a thousand horses and a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 上以慶則勳高，皆無所問。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Qingze’s merit was high, questioned none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qingze’s merit was great, the emperor asked nothing about it.

sentences.zh: 授上柱國，封魯國公，食任城縣千戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supreme Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Lu, with a sustenance fief of one thousand households in Rencheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Supreme Pillar of State, created Duke of Lu, with a sustenance fief of one thousand households in Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 詔以彭城公回授第二子義。

translations.literal: An edict returned the title Duke of Pengcheng and granted it to his second son Yi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict transferred the title Duke of Pengcheng to his second son Yi.

sentences.zh: 高祖平陳之後，幸晉王第，置酒會群臣。

translations.literal: After Emperor Gaozu pacified Chen, he visited the residence of the Prince of Jin, set out wine, and feasted the nobles and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Chen, the emperor visited the Prince of Jin’s residence and feasted the officials.

sentences.zh: 高熲等奉觴上壽，上因曰：「高熲平江南，虞慶則降突厥，可謂茂功矣。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong and others raised cups to offer longevity; the emperor thereupon said: "Gao Jiong pacified the lands south of the Yangtze; Yu Qingze made the Turks submit—this can be called abundant merit.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong and the others raised their cups in toast; the emperor said, "Gao Jiong conquered the south; Yu Qingze brought the Turks to submit—truly abundant merit.

sentences.zh: 」楊素曰：「皆由至尊威德所被。

translations.literal: " Yang Su said: "All is owing to Your Majesty’s majestic virtue spreading abroad.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Su said, "All of it rests on Your Majesty’s majestic virtue.

sentences.zh: 」慶則曰：「楊素前出兵武牢、硤石，若非至尊威德，亦無克理。

translations.literal: " Qingze said: "When Yang Su earlier led troops out at Wulao and Xiaoshi, if not for Your Majesty’s majestic virtue, there would likewise have been no principle of conquest.
translations.idiomatic: " Qingze said, "When Yang Su marched on Wulao and Xiaoshi, without Your Majesty’s virtue he could not have prevailed either.

sentences.zh: 」遂與互相長短。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they exchanged boasts of their strengths with each other.
translations.idiomatic: " They then traded boasts with one another.

sentences.zh: 御史欲彈之，上曰：「今日計功為樂，宜不須劾。

translations.literal: The censor wished to impeach them; the emperor said: "Today we count merit for joy—there is no need to impeach.
translations.idiomatic: A censor wished to impeach them; the emperor said, "Today we celebrate merit for pleasure—no impeachments.

sentences.zh: 」上觀群臣宴射，慶則進曰：「臣蒙賚酒食，令盡樂，御史在側，恐醉而被彈。

translations.literal: " The emperor watched the nobles and ministers feast and shoot; Qingze advanced and said: "Your servant has received bestowed wine and food and been ordered to enjoy fully; the censor is at the side—I fear drunkenness and being impeached.
translations.idiomatic: " As the emperor watched the officials feast and shoot, Qingze said, "Your Majesty has given me wine and ordered me to enjoy myself fully, but with a censor beside me I fear drunken impeachment.

sentences.zh: 」上賜御史酒，因遣之出。

translations.literal: " The emperor granted the censor wine and thereby sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor gave the censor wine and sent him out.

sentences.zh: 慶則奉觴上壽，極歡。

translations.literal: Qingze raised his cup to offer longevity with the utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: Qingze raised his cup in toast with the greatest merriment.

sentences.zh: 上謂諸公曰：「飲此酒，願我與諸公等子孫常如今日，世守富貴。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the nobles: "Drink this wine; I wish that I and you nobles’ sons and grandsons may always be as today, guarding wealth and honor through the generations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the nobles, "Drink this wine; may you and I and our sons and grandsons forever be as we are today, guarding wealth and honor through the ages.

sentences.zh: 」九年，轉為右衛大將軍，尋改為右武候大將軍。

translations.literal: " In the ninth year he was transferred to General of the Right Guards Army; shortly thereafter changed to General of the Right Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: " In year 9 he was made General of the Right Guards Army, then General of the Right Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 開皇十七年，嶺南人李賢據州反，高祖議欲討之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaihuang the man of Lingnan Li Xian seized a prefecture and rebelled; Emperor Gaozu deliberated wishing to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 17 Li Xian of Lingnan seized a prefecture and rebelled; the emperor planned to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 諸將二三請行，皆不許。

translations.literal: Two or three generals requested to go; none were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Two or three generals asked to go; none were allowed.

sentences.zh: 高祖顧謂慶則曰：「位居宰相，爵乃上公，國家有賊，遂無行意，何也？

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu turned and said to Qingze: "You hold the position of Chancellor and your rank is Supreme Duke—when the state has bandits, you then have no intent to go—why?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Qingze and said, "You are chancellor and a supreme duke—when the state has rebels you show no wish to march—why?

sentences.zh: 」慶則拜謝恐懼，上乃遣焉。

translations.literal: " Qingze bowed in thanks and fear; the emperor then dispatched him.
translations.idiomatic: " Qingze bowed in fear and thanks; the emperor then sent him.

sentences.zh: 為桂州道行軍總管，以婦弟趙什柱為隨府長史。

translations.literal: He was made Campaign Commander-in-Chief of the Guizhou Circuit, with his wife’s younger brother Zhao Shizhu as Chief Administrator of the accompanying staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was made campaign commander of the Guizhou circuit, with his wife’s younger brother Zhao Shizhu as chief administrator of his staff.

sentences.zh: 什柱先與慶則愛妾通，恐事彰，乃宣言曰：「慶則不欲此行。

translations.literal: Shizhu had earlier had relations with Qingze’s beloved concubine; fearing the affair would be exposed, he proclaimed: "Qingze does not wish this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhu had already slept with Qingze’s favorite concubine; fearing exposure, he spread word that Qingze did not want this campaign.

sentences.zh: 」遂聞於上。

translations.literal: " This reached the emperor’s ears.
translations.idiomatic: This reached the emperor.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝臣出征，上皆宴別，禮賜遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when court ministers went on campaign, the emperor always feasted them in farewell and ceremonially bestowed gifts as they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when court ministers departed on campaign, the emperor always gave a farewell feast and ceremonial gifts.

sentences.zh: 及慶則南討辭上，上色不悅，慶則由是怏怏不得志。

translations.literal: When Qingze took leave of the emperor for the southern campaign, the emperor’s expression was displeased; Qingze for this reason was resentful and unfulfilled in his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingze took leave for the southern campaign the emperor looked displeased, and Qingze left resentful and dispirited.

sentences.zh: 暨平賢，至潭州臨桂鎮，慶則觀眺山川形勢，曰：「此誠險固，加以足糧，若守得其人，攻不可拔。

translations.literal: When Xian was pacified, reaching Lingui Post in Tanzhou, Qingze surveyed the mountains and rivers and terrain, saying: "This is truly perilous and firm; add sufficient grain—if defended by the right man, it cannot be stormed.
translations.idiomatic: After Xian was pacified, at Lingui in Tanzhou, Qingze surveyed the terrain and said, "This place is truly strong; with enough grain and the right defender, it cannot be taken.

sentences.zh: 」遂使什柱馳詣京奏事，觀上顏色。

translations.literal: " He then had Shizhu ride post-horses to the capital to report affairs and observe the emperor’s expression.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Shizhu by relay horse to the capital to report affairs and read the emperor’s mood.

sentences.zh: 什柱至京，因告慶則謀反。

translations.literal: When Shizhu reached the capital, he reported that Qingze plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Shizhu reported that Qingze was plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上案驗之，慶則於是伏誅。

translations.literal: The emperor investigated and verified it; Qingze thereupon confessed and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor investigated and Qingze confessed and was executed.

sentences.zh: 拜什柱為柱國。

translations.literal: Shizhu was appointed Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhu was made Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 慶則子孝仁，幼豪俠任氣，起家拜儀同，領晉王親信。

translations.literal: Qingze’s son Xiaoren in youth was bold, chivalrous, and willful; he began his career appointed Yitong and led the Prince of Jin’s trusted followers.
translations.idiomatic: Qingze’s son Xiaoren was bold and willful from youth; he began as Yitong and led the Prince of Jin’s trusted followers.

sentences.zh: 坐父事除名。

translations.literal: He was implicated in his father’s affair and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was struck from the rolls because of his father’s crime.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，以籓邸之舊，授候衛長史，兼領金穀監，監禁苑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, because of old ties from the princely residence, he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Palace Guards, and concurrently directed the Gold and Grain Office, supervising the forbidden park.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, because of old ties from his days as prince, Xiaoren was made chief administrator of the palace guards and overseer of the forbidden park and treasury.

sentences.zh: 有巧思，頗稱旨。

translations.literal: He had ingenious ideas and largely accorded with the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: He had ingenious ideas and pleased the emperor greatly.

sentences.zh: 九年，伐遼，授都水丞，充使監運，頗有功。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, in the campaign against Liao, he was appointed Assistant Director of Waterways, serving as envoy to supervise transport, with considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, during the Liaodong campaign, he was made Assistant Director of Waterways and supervised transport with considerable merit.

sentences.zh: 然性奢華，以駱駝負函盛水養魚而自給。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was luxurious; he used camels to carry boxes filled with water to raise fish for his own supply.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was luxurious by nature and used camels to carry boxes of water so he could raise fish for his own table.

sentences.zh: 十一年，或告孝仁謀圖不軌，遂誅之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year someone reported that Xiaoren plotted irregular conduct; he was thereupon executed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 someone reported that Xiaoren was plotting rebellion, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 其弟澄道，東宮通事舍人，坐除名。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chengdong was an Attendant Master of Affairs of the Eastern Palace; he was implicated and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chengdong, an attendant of the Eastern Palace, was also struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 元胄元胄，河南洛陽人也，魏昭成帝之六代孫。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhou—Yuan Zhou was a man of Luoyang in Henan, sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhou came from Luoyang in Henan, a sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖順，魏濮陽王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shun was Prince of Puyang of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shun had been Prince of Puyang under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父雄，武陵王。

translations.literal: His father Xiong was Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiong had been Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 胄少英果，多武藝，美鬚眉，有不可犯之色。

translations.literal: Zhou in youth was heroic and resolute, skilled in many martial arts, with handsome beard and brows and a bearing that could not be violated.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Zhou was bold and resolute, skilled in arms, handsome of beard and brow, with a bearing no one dared offend.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲見而壯之，引致左右，數從征伐。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou saw him and considered him stalwart, brought him to attend at left and right, and he repeatedly followed on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi saw him, admired his strength, took him into his service, and he followed on many campaigns.

sentences.zh: 官至大將軍。

translations.literal: His office reached Great General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Great General.

sentences.zh: 高祖初被召入，將受顧托，先呼胄，次命陶澄，並委以腹心，恆宿臥內。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was first summoned in, about to receive the dying entrustment, he first called Zhou, then ordered Tao Cheng, and entrusted both with his innermost heart; they constantly lodged within the sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was first summoned to the dying emperor’s side, he called Zhou first, then Tao Cheng, and entrusted both with his innermost counsel; they slept constantly in the inner apartments.

sentences.zh: 及為丞相，每典軍在禁中，又引弟威俱入侍衛。

translations.literal: When he became Chancellor, he always commanded armies within the forbidden precincts and also brought in his younger brother Wei together to serve as guards.
translations.idiomatic: When he became chancellor he commanded troops within the palace and brought his younger brother Wei in as guard as well.

sentences.zh: 周趙王招知高祖將遷周鼎，乃要高祖就第。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao of Zhou, Zhao, knowing that Emperor Gaozu was about to move the Zhou tripod, then requested that Gaozu come to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao of Zhou, knowing Yang Jian meant to seize the Zhou throne, invited him to his residence.

sentences.zh: 趙王引高祖入寢室，左右不得從，唯楊弘與胄兄弟坐于戶側。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao led Gaozu into the sleeping chamber; attendants at left and right could not follow; only Yang Hong and the Zhou brothers sat at the side of the door.
translations.idiomatic: The prince led Yang Jian into his bedchamber; attendants could not follow; only Yang Hong and the Zhou brothers sat by the door.

sentences.zh: 趙王謂其二子員、貫曰：「汝當進瓜，我因刺殺之。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao said to his two sons Yuan and Guan: "You should present melon; I will thereby stab and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince told his sons Yuan and Guan, "Bring in the melon; I shall stab him then.

sentences.zh: 」及酒酣，趙王欲生變，以佩刀子刺瓜，連啖高祖，將為不利。

translations.literal: " When the wine was deep, Prince Zhao wished to create a disturbance; with his belt knife he stabbed the melon and repeatedly urged Gaozu to eat, intending harm.
translations.idiomatic: " When the wine was deep the prince meant to strike; he stabbed the melon with his belt knife and pressed Yang Jian to eat, intending harm.

sentences.zh: 胄進曰：「相府有事，不可久留。

translations.literal: Zhou advanced and said: "The Chancellor’s office has business; you cannot stay long.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou stepped forward and said, "The chancellor’s office has urgent business; you cannot stay long.

sentences.zh: 」趙王訶之曰：「我與丞相言，汝何為者！

translations.literal: " Prince Zhao rebuked him, saying: "I am speaking with the Chancellor—what are you doing!
translations.idiomatic: " The prince rebuked him, "I am speaking with the chancellor—what are you doing!

sentences.zh: 」叱之使卻。

translations.literal: " He shouted at him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: " He shouted at him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 胄瞋目憤氣，扣刀入衛。

translations.literal: Zhou glared with angry spirit, grasped his knife, and entered as guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou glared in fury, hand on his knife, and entered to guard Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 趙王問其姓名，胄以實對。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao asked his name; Zhou answered truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked his name; Zhou answered truthfully.

sentences.zh: 趙王曰：「汝非昔事齊王者乎？

translations.literal: Prince Zhao said: "Are you not the one who formerly served the Prince of Qi?
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Were you not once in the service of Prince Xian of Qi?

sentences.zh: 誠壯士也！

translations.literal: Truly a stalwart man!
translations.idiomatic: A true champion!

sentences.zh: 」因賜之酒，曰：「吾豈有不善之意邪？

translations.literal: " He thereupon granted him wine, saying: "How could I have ill intent?
translations.idiomatic: " He gave him wine and said, "How could I mean you harm?

sentences.zh: 卿何猜警如是！

translations.literal: Why are you so suspicious and on guard!
translations.idiomatic: Why are you so suspicious!

sentences.zh: 」趙王偽吐，將入後閤，胄恐其為變，扶令上坐，如此者再三。

translations.literal: " Prince Zhao pretended to vomit and was about to enter the rear chamber; Zhou feared he would create a disturbance, supported him and made him sit above, doing this three times.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince pretended to vomit and meant to enter the rear chamber; Zhou feared a coup, helped him back to his seat, and did this three times.

sentences.zh: 趙王稱喉幹，命胄就廚取飲，胄不動。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao said his throat was dry and ordered Zhou to go to the kitchen for drink; Zhou did not move.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said his throat was dry and ordered Zhou to the kitchen for drink; Zhou did not move.

sentences.zh: 會滕王逌後至，高祖降階迎之，胄與高祖耳語曰：「事勢大異，可速去。

translations.literal: When Prince Teng You arrived later, Gaozu descended the steps to welcome him; Zhou whispered in Gaozu’s ear: "The situation is greatly changed—you can leave quickly.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Teng You arrived, Yang Jian went down to welcome him; Zhou whispered, "The situation has changed utterly—leave at once.

sentences.zh: 」高祖猶不悟，謂曰：「彼無兵馬，複何能為？

translations.literal: " Gaozu still did not understand and said: "He has no troops and horses—what more can he do?
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Jian still did not understand and said, "He has no troops—what can he do?

sentences.zh: 」胄曰：「兵馬悉他家物，一先下手，大事便去。

translations.literal: " Zhou said: "Troops and horses are all his household’s property—if he strikes first, the great affair is gone.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou said, "His household guards are at hand—if he strikes first, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 胄不辭死，死何益耶？

translations.literal: Zhou does not decline death—but what good is death?
translations.idiomatic: I do not fear death—but what good is dying here?

sentences.zh: 」高祖複入坐。

translations.literal: " Gaozu again entered and sat.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Jian sat down again.

sentences.zh: 胄聞屋後有被甲聲，遽請曰：「相府事殷，公何得如此？

translations.literal: Zhou heard the sound of armor behind the house and urgently requested: "The Chancellor’s office has pressing business—how can you, sir, be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou heard armor behind the house and said urgently, "The chancellor’s office is pressed with business—how can you linger?

sentences.zh: 」因扶高祖下床，趣而去。

translations.literal: " He thereupon supported Gaozu off the bed and hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: " He helped Yang Jian from the couch and hurried him away.

sentences.zh: 趙王將追之，胄以身蔽戶，王不得出。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao was about to pursue; Zhou blocked the door with his body; the prince could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: The prince tried to pursue; Zhou blocked the door with his body and the prince could not pass.

sentences.zh: 高祖及門，胄自後而至。

translations.literal: When Gaozu reached the gate, Zhou came from behind and arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian reached the gate, Zhou caught up from behind.

sentences.zh: 趙王恨不時發，彈指出血。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao hated that he had not struck in time; he flicked his finger until blood came out.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, bitter that he had not struck in time, flicked his finger until it bled.

sentences.zh: 及誅趙王，賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao was executed, rewards and gifts were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhao was executed, the rewards given Zhou were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進位上柱國，封武陵郡公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was advanced to Supreme Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuling Commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Zhou was made Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Wuling with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 拜左衛將軍，尋遷右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Left Guards Army; shortly thereafter transferred to General of the Right Guards Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Left Guards Army, then General of the Right Guards Army.

sentences.zh: 高祖從容曰：「保護朕躬，成此基業，元胄功也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said at ease: "Protecting my person and accomplishing this foundation—this is Yuan Zhou’s merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said calmly, "Protecting my person and establishing this foundation—that was Yuan Zhou’s merit.

sentences.zh: 」後數載，出為豫州刺史，曆亳、淅二州刺史。

translations.literal: " Several years later he was sent out as Governor of Yuzhou and served as Governor of Bozhou and Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Several years later he served as governor of Yuzhou, Bozhou, and Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為邊患，朝廷以胄素有威名，拜靈州總管，北夷甚憚焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly became border troubles; the court, because Zhou had long had a formidable reputation, appointed him Commander-in-Chief of Lingzhou; the northern barbarians feared him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks repeatedly troubled the border, the court, knowing Zhou’s formidable reputation, made him supreme commander of Lingzhou, and the northern tribes feared him greatly.

sentences.zh: 後複征為右衛大將軍，親顧益密。

translations.literal: Later he was again summoned as General of the Right Guards Army; personal regard grew ever closer.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as General of the Right Guards Army, and the emperor’s favor toward him only deepened.

sentences.zh: 嘗正月十五日，上與近臣登高，時胄下直，上令馳召之。

translations.literal: Once on the fifteenth day of the first month the emperor climbed high with close ministers; at that time Zhou was off duty; the emperor ordered him summoned by relay horse.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the Lantern Festival the emperor climbed high with his intimates; Zhou was off duty, and the emperor sent a relay horse to summon him.

sentences.zh: 及胄見，上謂曰：「公與外人登高，未若就朕勝也。

translations.literal: When Zhou appeared, the emperor said: "You, sir, climbing high with outsiders is not equal to coming to me—it is better.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou arrived the emperor said, "Climbing high with others is not as fine as climbing with me.

sentences.zh: 」賜宴極歡。

translations.literal: " He granted a feast of the utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave a feast of the greatest intimacy.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣每致禮焉。

translations.literal: Prince Jin Guang always sent him courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guang of Jin always paid him courtesy.

sentences.zh: 房陵王之廢也，胄豫其謀。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fangling was deposed, Zhou took part in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fangling was deposed, Zhou took part in the plot.

sentences.zh: 上正窮治東宮事，左衛大將軍元旻苦諫，楊素乃譖之。

translations.literal: The emperor was then exhaustively investigating affairs of the Eastern Palace; Left Guards General Yuan Min remonstrated bitterly; Yang Su then slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was investigating the Eastern Palace affair, Left Guards General Yuan Min remonstrated bitterly; Yang Su slandered him.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，執旻於仗。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and seized Min at the staff of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and seized Min at the palace.

sentences.zh: 胄時當下直，不去，因奏曰：「臣不下直者，為防元旻耳。

translations.literal: Zhou at that time should have gone off duty but did not leave; he thereupon memorialized, saying: "Your servant does not go off duty in order to guard against Yuan Min.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou should have gone off duty but stayed and said, "I have not left my post because I am guarding against Yuan Min.

sentences.zh: 」複以此言激怒上，上遂誅旻，賜胄帛千匹。

translations.literal: " Again with these words he enraged the emperor; the emperor thereupon executed Min and granted Zhou a thousand lengths of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " These words enraged the emperor further; he executed Min and gave Zhou a thousand lengths of silk.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀之得罪，胄坐與交通，除名。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shu Xiu incurred guilt, Zhou was implicated for dealings with him and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shu Xiu fell from favor, Zhou was implicated for dealings with him and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，不得調。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, he received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 時慈州刺史上官政坐事徙嶺南，將軍丘和亦以罪廢。

translations.literal: At that time the Governor of Cizhou Shangguan Zheng was implicated in an affair and banished to Lingnan; the general Qiu He was also dismissed for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Governor Shangguan Zheng of Cizhou was banished to the south for an offense, and General Qiu He was dismissed for a crime as well.

sentences.zh: 胄與和有舊，因數從之遊。

translations.literal: Zhou had old ties with He and therefore frequently followed him in his wanderings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had old ties with He and often kept him company.

sentences.zh: 胄嘗酒酣謂和曰：「上官政壯士也，今徙嶺表，得無大事乎？

translations.literal: Zhou once, when wine was deep, said to He: "Shangguan Zheng is a stalwart man; now he is banished beyond the Ling range—might there not be a great affair?
translations.idiomatic: Once when drunk Zhou said to He, "Shangguan Zheng is a true champion; banished beyond the Ling range, might he not stir up great trouble?

sentences.zh: 」因自拊腹曰：「若是公者，不徒然矣。

translations.literal: " He thereupon slapped his own belly and said: "If it were you, sir, it would not be in vain.
translations.idiomatic: " He slapped his belly and said, "If it were you, sir, it would not be for nothing.

sentences.zh: 」和明日奏之，胄竟坐死。

translations.literal: " The next day He reported it; Zhou in the end was implicated and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He reported this the next day, and Zhou was executed.

sentences.zh: 於是征政為驍衛將軍，拜和代州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zheng was summoned as General of the Valiant Guards Army; He was appointed Governor of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was then summoned as General of the Valiant Guards, and He was made governor of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 史評史臣曰：昔韓信愆垓下之期，則項王不滅；

translations.literal: Historical judgment—the historiographer says: In former times, if Han Xin had not missed the appointment below Gaixia, the King of Xiang would not have perished;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer comments: In former times, had Han Xin not missed his rendezvous below Gaixia, the King of Xiang would not have fallen;

sentences.zh: 英布無淮南之舉，則漢道未隆。

translations.literal: if Ying Bu had made no rising in Huainan, the Way of Han would not have risen to eminence.
translations.idiomatic: had Ying Bu not risen in Huainan, the house of Han would not have risen to greatness.

sentences.zh: 以二子之勳庸，鹹憤怨而菹戮，況乃無古人之殊績，而懷悖逆之心者乎！

translations.literal: With the merit and service of these two men, all were resentful and dismembered in the pickle tub—how much more those who lack the extraordinary achievements of the ancients yet harbor rebellious hearts!
translations.idiomatic: Men of such merit were cut down in resentment—how much more those who lacked the ancients’ extraordinary deeds yet harbored treason in their hearts!

sentences.zh: 梁士彥、宇文忻皆一時之壯士也，遭雲雷之會，並以勇略成名，遂貪天之功以為己力。

translations.literal: Liang Shiyan and Yu Wenxin were both stalwart men of their age; they encountered the meeting of cloud and thunder, both made names through courage and strategy, and then coveted heaven’s merit as their own strength.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shiyan and Yu Wenxin were champions of their age; they rose in the storm of founding and won fame by courage and strategy, then claimed heaven’s merit as their own.

sentences.zh: 報者倦矣，施者未厭，將生厲階，求逞其欲，及茲顛墜，自取之也。

translations.literal: Those who repay are weary; those who bestow are not yet sated; they would breed dangerous steps and seek to indulge their desires—when they toppled at this point, they brought it on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had repaid them grew weary while the throne was not yet sated; they bred trouble and sought their desires—and when they fell, they had brought it on themselves.

sentences.zh: 王誼、元諧、王世積、虞慶則、元胄，或契闊艱厄，或綢繆恩舊，將安將樂，漸見遺忘，內懷怏怏，矜伐不已。

translations.literal: Wang Yi, Yuan Xie, Wang Shiji, Yu Qingze, and Yuan Zhou—some had shared hardship in peril, some had been bound in old favor; when peace and joy were at hand they were gradually forgotten; inwardly they harbored resentment and ceaselessly boasted of their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, Yuan Xie, Wang Shiji, Yu Qingze, and Yuan Zhou—some had shared hardship in the founding, some had been bound by old friendship; when peace came they were gradually forgotten, nursed resentment within, and boasted of their merit without end.

sentences.zh: 雖時主之刻薄，亦言語以速禍乎？

translations.literal: Though the ruler of the age was harsh, did they also hasten calamity through their words?
translations.idiomatic: Though the ruler of the age was harsh, did they not also hasten their doom through their own words?

sentences.zh: 然高祖佐命元功，鮮有終其天命，配享清廟，寂寞無聞。

translations.literal: Yet among Emperor Gaozu’s founding merit-holders who aided the Mandate, few completed their heaven-appointed span, received sacrifice in the clear temple, and were not left lonely and unheard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet of the founding merit-holders who aided Yang Jian, few lived out their natural span or received sacrifice in the imperial temple—most passed into lonely obscurity.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋草創帝圖，事出權道，本異同心，故久而逾薄。

translations.literal: This was because in the first establishment of the imperial design affairs arose from expedient ways; they were originally not of one heart—therefore as time lengthened affection grew ever thinner.
translations.idiomatic: This was because in founding the empire affairs arose from expedient measures; they had never been of one heart, and so as time passed favor grew ever thinner.

sentences.zh: 其牽牛蹊田，雖則有罪，奪之非道，能無怨乎？

translations.literal: When one leads an ox across another’s field, though there is guilt, to seize it by an unjust way—can there be no resentment?
translations.idiomatic: To lead an ox across another’s field is wrong—but to seize it unjustly, can there be no resentment?

sentences.zh: 皆深文巧詆，致之刑辟，高祖沉猜之心，固已甚矣。

translations.literal: All were prosecuted with deep statutes and crafty slander, brought to criminal punishment; Emperor Gaozu’s deep and suspicious heart was already very severe.
translations.idiomatic: All were prosecuted with twisted statutes and crafty slander and brought to execution; Yang Jian’s deep suspicion was already extreme.

sentences.zh: 求其餘慶，不亦難哉！

translations.literal: To seek their remaining good fortune—is it not also difficult!
translations.idiomatic: To expect any remaining blessing for their lines—was that not also difficult!
